ve_generic: Vertical exaggeration (VE, slider 1-5x, default 1x, always displayed in the viewer) multiplies every height (water, seabed, reef) and never a plan distance: tan(apparent angle) = VE x tan(true angle). Every number on this page is a true (1x) value. Photo-match mode forces VE = 1.

models.name: Borth coastal defence reef (incl. Wallog headland)
models.model_name: Borth coastal defence reef (Phase 1, Ceredigion, Wales)
models.state_short: As built, Phase 1 completed 8 March 2012: the northern boot-shaped SURF REEF and the southern oval BREAKWATER (a shore-parallel breakwater, not a surf reef), rock mounds on the seabed. Default outline = the 2022 LiDAR laser-survey edge; two more outline versions are offered.

confidence.reason: The plan shape is high-confidence, and the rock surface above the water edge is a 1 m laser survey that agrees with the design crests within about 0.3 m. The seabed is the weak link: the design drawings show a typical bed level of about -4.0 mODN (beds "vary"), the HRPP576 Fig 2 contours are read by eye (+-0.5 m), and the mean-sea-level offset of +0.31 mODN is a four-level estimate (+-0.15 m), so reef height above the bed is known to about +-0.5 m and volumes to about +-15 %.

caveats.q: Volume (rock)
caveats.model: 30,119 m3 laser edge / 28,919 m3 design foot / 25,504 m3 photo edge (+-4,600 m3 for 0.4 m of bed)
caveats.stated: no reef-only quantity at a primary source; Type 4 for the whole Phase 1: 42,000 t (NCE)
caveats.diff: default Type 4 layer about 36,100 t, below 42,000 t
caveats.reason: Volume = crest surface minus the modelled seabed. Only the bed under the rock matters, and it is a design level (-4.0 mODN derived); the three outline versions differ by up to 15 %.
caveats.resolve: A reef-only rock quantity from the contractor; a low-tide multibeam or imagery of the flanks below -2.3 mODN.

caveats.q: Offshore seabed (y > 335 m) versus the Fig 2 -4.0 m contour
caveats.model: follows the Fig 2 -4.0 m contour (traced nodes, plus assumed bridge and extension nodes); beyond it the EMODnet gradient -1.1 % (mODN)
caveats.stated: HRPP576 Fig 2: -4.0 m contour at y 410-460 m; EMODnet cells 0.7-1.2 m shallower; Navionics chart zero -3.58 mODN
caveats.diff: 0.00 m at the 13 traced points (was 0.89 m deeper before the D6 fix of 2026-10-07)
caveats.reason: The first build evaluated the seabed fit at y <= 335 m only and used an assumed -4.0 m anchor there, so it ignored the Fig 2 -4.0 m contour and the design bed nodes under the arm head. The D6 fix (option B) makes the contour a control; the bed under the arm head rose up to 0.7 m and the rock volumes fell 3.4-3.9 %.
caveats.resolve: Done (D6, 2026-10-07). Remaining: the -4.0 m level is bridged / extended by assumption at x -104..170 and x > 170; a sounding line or multibeam seaward of the reef would test it.

caveats.q: Length of the oval breakwater (38 m or 46 m)
caveats.model: 38 m (setting-out table of drawing 1020; the plan strip measures 38 m)
caveats.stated: 46 m (drawing 1023, 23,000 + 23,000 mm between R15 and R14)
caveats.diff: -8 m, about 2 % of the oval volume
caveats.reason: Two drawings of the same rev C1 set disagree.
caveats.resolve: The contractor's as-built setting-out table.
ev: 23,000 + 23,000 mm between SOP R15 and R14 (46 m)

gallery.how_used: Measured (values only; the tile is not kept in the project): exposed footprint N 5861 m2 and S 2814 m2; DSM crest p90 +0.72 mODN on the northern arm, +1.0..+1.15 near the tail, +1.5 on the oval (design +0.50 / +1.00 / +1.50); mean flank slope 1:4.4 (-1.5..-0.5 mODN) and 1:5.3 (-0.5..+0.2), flatter than the design 1:3; width at -2.3 mODN 34-37 m (arm), 50 m (head), 38-41 m (oval). models.methods_html:
METHODS_3D - Borth coastal defence reef (Phase 1, Ceredigion, Wales)

3D model v1, 2026-10-07 (3D agent, Sonnet 5.5); seabed fix D6 applied 2026-10-07 (3.3; model v1.1; the pre-fix files are in 3d\archive\pre_D6\). Files: 3d\model.js (data), 3d\index.html (viewer), 3d\build_3d.py (rebuilds model.js, docs.js and, with --shape, shape.json), 3d\make_annotations.py and 3d\nav_read.py (annotated images), 3d\SOURCES_3D.md (step-by-step log). Not for navigation.

1. Summary

The model shows the as-built final layout of Borth Phase 1 (completed 8 March 2012): a northern boot-shaped surf reef (crest +0.50 mODN, tail +1.00, head edge +0.00 rising over about 40 m) and a southern oval that is a shore-parallel breakwater, not a surf reef (crest +1.50 mODN), on a seabed rebuilt from the 2022 LiDAR beach, the HRPP576 Fig 2 contours, the design bed levels and the EMODnet trend, with the water surface selectable from LAT to MHWS. Three outlines of the same structure are modelled and selectable: the laser-survey edge (Welsh Government LiDAR, 19 Mar 2022, 8,675 m2, default, chosen by Lior on 2026-10-06), the design rock-layer foot of drawing 9V5090/1020 (Jan 2011, 6,989 m2) and the visible rock edge in the Esri photo of 17 Sep 2024 (5,743 m2). The default surface is the 1 m LiDAR DSM above the exposed level (about -2.3 mODN) plus the design toe berm and blanket of drawings 1021-1023 below it; the model rock volume is 30,100 m3 (about 51,200 t at 1.7 t/m3, +-15 %). No later damage, deflation or removal was found (imagery 2012-2024, 2022 LiDAR), so no second state is modelled. 3D confidence: MEDIUM: the plan and the crest levels are well supported (laser survey and design agree within 0.3 m), but the seabed under and around the rock rests on a design bed level (about -4.0 mODN, "bed levels vary"), a hand-read contour figure and an estimated MSL offset, and the sea floor seaward of the reef now follows the Fig 2 -4.0 contour (fixed on 2026-10-07: it had been 0.89 m deeper than that contour, sections 3.3 and 4.4), so heights above the bed are known to about +-0.5 m and volumes to about +-15 %.

2. Data sources

Source audit 2026-10-10: the full register (what was read off each source, how, accuracy, model element), the methods list, assumptions A1-A14 with effect and replacement, decisions DEC1-DEC14 and confidence per element are in REGISTER_3D.md (viewer: Methods tab, second button). The table below is the original source list; the registry now has 31 rows (img-31 = Blacka et al. 2013, Fig 4.1).

Citations are author-year; "id" is the source id used in model.js provenance and shape.json. Registry ids refer to 03_images\reefs\borth-coastal-defence-reef\images.json. All local copies are private research copies; reuse rights are to be checked before any public release.

3. Methods

3.1 Frame and datums

  • Canonical frame of shape.json (metres): x alongshore, + toward SOUTH (bearing 179.57 deg); y offshore, + toward WEST (bearing 269.57 deg); origin at the foot of the perpendicular from the centroid of both mounds on the defence line (back of the shingle beach, bearing 359.57 deg). z up.
  • OS grid to canonical is an affine map fitted over a 600 x 600 m window to the exact chain (OSGB36 -> WGS84 Helmert via pyproj -> local tangent plane -> rotation): residual rms 0.005 m, max 0.02 m (b3d_lib.Frame). Absolute position is limited by the Helmert (+-2-5 m), not by this fit.
  • Vertical: working datum Ordnance Datum Newlyn (ODN = mAOD). Model zero = mean sea level:
z_MSL = z_ODN - 0.31                     (E1)  MSL = +0.31 mODN = (MLWS + MLWN + MHWN + MHWS)/4, +-0.15 m  (A2)
z_LAT = z_ODN + 2.44      (depth below chart datum d_CD = -(z_ODN + 2.44) for the sea floor)   (E2)  LAT = -2.44 mODN (A3)
z_MSL = e_LAT - 2.75                     (E3)  EMODnet cells are given relative to LAT

3.2 Reef surface, three versions (1 m grid, window x -105..150, y 235..420 m)

Common design constants (drawings 1021-1023): crest +0.50 (arm, 9 m wide), +1.00 (tail, strip R2/R5-R3/R4, transition 15 m from SOP R2), +0.00 at the head edge (R1/R10) rising to +0.50 over about 40 m, +1.50 (oval, flat top 6 m x 38-46 m between R14 and R15); Type 4 layer 2.70 m thick; toe berm 1.35 m high, 3 m top, 1:1.5 sides; flat apron 2.0 m; blanket 0.5 m with 1:1.5 edge; foot of the Type 4 slope = top of the toe berm = -2.15 mODN (bed -4.0 + blanket 0.5 + berm 1.35).

  • design_1020 (Royal Haskoning rock-layer foot). Concentric rings 0-4 of drawing 1020 are extracted from the vector PDF and georeferenced with the 15 setting-out points. Between rings the surface is interpolated linearly in the distance to the two bounding rings: ring 0 (apron outer edge) at the seabed -> ring 1 (blanket top edge, +0.5 m) -> ring 2 -> ring 3 (berm top outer edge) -> ring 4 at -2.15; inside ring 4 the surface rises linearly in distance to the crest outline (R1-R6, R2-R5 paths, crest zones with the heights above) at the crest height of the zone. The 1:3 / 1:4 / 1:5 slopes are therefore not imposed separately; they result from ring spacing (the plan is drawn to those slopes). Surface = max(design, seabed).
  • lidar_2022 (default). Inside the outline of the exposed rock (cells with a LiDAR return, water edge about -2.3 mODN, 1 m cells, simplified 0.4 m) the surface is the LiDAR DSM, lightly smoothed (normalised Gaussian, sigma 0.8 m, A9) and never below the edge level; outside the outline the design toe is attached with the same toe slopes as drawings 1021-1023: 1:1.5 down from the edge level to the blanket top (bed + 0.5 m), 2 m flat apron, 1:1.5 blanket edge to the seabed (A11). The surface below the water edge is therefore design, not measured.
  • sat_2024 (visible rock edge). The same construction with the 79-vertex outline traced on the 2024 Esri image and edge level -1.3 mODN. Because the toe slope is imposed from the edge (1:1.5) it is steeper than the real flanks and the volume is smaller.
  • Zones for colour: 1 armour / surveyed surface (Type 4), 2 toe berm (Type 0), 3 blanket and apron (Type 6).
  • Rock volume is the integral of (surface - modelled seabed) over the 1 m grid, both mounds, including berm and blanket. Type-4-layer volume is the integral of min(2.70 m, surface - bed) over the armour zone. Tonnes = volume x 1.7 t/m3 (A8).

D6 fix, 2026-10-07 (bug fix of the seabed outside the reef; model v1 -> v1.1). Two faults of the first build are removed:

  1. Cause. seabed_grid evaluated the thin-plate fit at min(y, 335) (the former ANCHOR_Y) and subtracted the EMODnet gradient beyond it. Why the volumes changed, and why that is accepted. The brief for the fix asked for unchanged volumes, on the belief that the design nodes already pinned the bed under the rock. They did not: the nodes at y > 335 m were ignored (fault 1), so the bed under the head of the arm (y 335-397 m) was up to 0.7 m too deep and the total volumes were overstated by 3.4-3.9 %. The coordinator therefore replaced the rule "volumes unchanged" by "volumes change only through the bed-node fix, documented" (2026-10-07). Option A (rejected): freeze the bed under the rock at the old values to keep the numbers. It would keep a pit under the arm head, up to 0.7 m deeper than both the design bed (-4.0) that the documentation states and the new sea floor around it. Option B (applied) makes the model agree with its own documentation. The bed under the rock is still a design level (+-0.4 m, section 5); the volume uncertainty (E9) is unchanged in kind.

New residuals to know. (a) The design bed under the arm (-4.0 at y 310-385) is 0.2-0.6 m deeper than a straight interpolation of the Fig 2 contours at the same place (-3.0 at y about 290, -4.0 at y about 415: -3.4 at y 335, -3.8 at y 385); the fit lets the bed rise from the design level to the Fig 2 level within about 40 m of the reef zone. Both are inside +-0.5 m. (b) The model is still 0.7-1.2 m deeper than the EMODnet absolute cells at y 368-513 (the cells are GEBCO-interpolated and are not used) and its implied Navionics zero (-3.75) is 0.17 m deeper than that implied by the Fig 2 -4.0 contour (-3.58). (c) The -4.0 level between x -104 and 170 and east of x 170 is bridged / extended by assumption (9 nodes); it lies 70 m or more from the rock. (d) A small ridge of 0.05-0.18 m per 5 m cell at y 340-345, x 160-260, comes from the oval nodes (-4.2 at y 340); it is inside the bed uncertainty.

3.4 Tides, water surface, viewer

The water is a horizontal plane at the selected level (static still water; no wave set-up, run-up or surf). The viewer shows seabed (coloured by depth), reef (coloured by zone), the water plane at 38 % opacity, a 10 m grid (50 m bold), 10 m and 50 m scale bars, a north arrow, the defence line y = 0, an outline of the selected version at its edge level, and a camera read-out (position, true heading, pitch, field of view). Vertical exaggeration 1-5 x (default 1) multiplies z only and is always shown; presets: oblique from the sea, plan (north to the left), along the surf-reef crest, from the beach at eye height 1.7 m, side view. Photo-match mode: a local image is overlaid on the canvas and camera x, y, z, true heading, pitch and field of view are adjusted until the rock outlines line up; "Copy camera" prints the parameters (vertical exaggeration forced to 1). Version selector with an (i) pop-up (versions_info plus a table name | date | source | footprint | volume); #version=<id> in the URL selects a version; #water=, #ve=, #view= also work.

LAT is the best standard datum against all three references and the one drying-height label agrees with it (0.2 m above chart datum = -2.24 mODN; the LiDAR has water there at -2.3: within 0.1 m), so the chart datum is taken as LAT (A13). The chart is therefore a cross-check only and was not used to build the seabed.

Crest and height. The structure still exists (LiDAR 2022; imagery to 2024) but it is not resolved by either layer: the rock mounds (0 to +1.5 mODN, 2.4-4 m above LAT) lie inside the uniformly green drying area with no symbol, label or contour at the footprint. The only charted shoal (closed 0.5 and 1 m loops) is at canonical (37, 405), 35 m seaward of the nearest rock, and is not the reef. Navionics therefore gives no crest depth or height, and no cross-check of the design figures was possible.

dV = 0.4 m x A(footprint incl. toe) = 0.4 x 11,391 = 4,556 m3 (15 %); density 1.6-1.8 t/m3 -> +-6 %; edge-level choice: +-8 % (section 4.1)    (E9)

Position: +-5 m (Esri), +-2-5 m (Helmert); horizontal seabed contours +-10 m. The sea floor outside the reef is less certain than under it: it follows the Fig 2 -3.0 and -4.0 contours (+-0.5 m, +-10 m) and, beyond the -4.0 contour, the EMODnet gradient; at y 370-515 m it is 0.7-1.2 m deeper than the EMODnet cells and about 1.3 m deeper than the Navionics chart zero (LAT) implies (section 4.4; before the D6 fix 0.9 m deeper than Fig 2 itself). Vertical exaggeration k multiplies every height and every slope in the picture by k while plan distances stay true; at k = 5 the 1:4 flanks look like 1:0.8. Heights, slopes and tide read-outs on screen are always true values (divided by k); the photo-match mode forces k = 1.

6. Confidence

MEDIUM. Against the project rubric (high = every input sourced and cross-checked within about 10 %, medium = key inputs sourced but at least one first-order input estimated, low = a first-order input missing): the plan is high (design rings and laser survey agree to 1 pixel / 0.3 m), the crest levels are high (three independent readings: design drawing, LiDAR, section drawings), the tide offsets are medium (MSL is a four-level estimate +-0.15 m, LAT from neighbouring ports), and the seabed is medium-low: under the rock it is the drawing-derived -4.0 mODN (+-0.4 m), around the rock a hand-read contour figure (-3.0 and -4.0 contours are controls since D6), and seaward of the -4.0 contour (y 408-473 m) an EMODnet gradient that sits 0.7-1.2 m deeper than the EMODnet cells themselves. Because the first-order unknown for "height above the bed" and for the volume is the bed level, the overall level is medium.

models.requests_html:
REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR - Borth coastal defence reef 3D model (2026-10-07)

Nothing here blocks the model; it is built with the stated assumptions. Each row is something I could not read myself. Coordinates are WGS84 decimal degrees (canonical x, y in brackets: x alongshore + south, y offshore + west, metres; computed from the OS-grid frame, +-5 m). Please note the units and the datum shown by the app next to each reading.

# tool exact lat / lon (canonical x, y) what to read datum / units to note why it matters for the model
1 Navionics app (SonarChart live, Nautical Chart) 52.483803, -4.056246 (-39, 333) north arm crest; 52.482690, -4.056129 (85, 326) oval centre Is there any symbol or label at the rock (obstruction, wreck / artificial reef, "FISH HAVEN", a drying height)? Read its text and depth/height app depth units (m or ft), datum if stated (Settings > Depth, "Chart datum") the web viewer shows nothing at the reef (inside a uniform drying area); the app may carry the structure as an obstruction and give an independent crest height
2 Navionics app 52.483538, -4.057231 (-10, 400); 52.483715, -4.057823 (-30, 440); 52.483710, -4.058900 (-30, 513); 52.483704, -4.060184 (-30, 600) spot depth (tap) at each point, and whether the depth contours 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 / 2 m cross the same places as in the web viewer (web viewer: 0 m line at y 385-430, 1 m about 105 m farther offshore) units and datum; time of day / tide if the app shows a tide correction the web chart is 1.1 m shallower than HRPP576 Fig 2 and 0.6 m shallower than EMODnet seaward of the reef, and the model is 0.9 m deeper than Fig 2 there: one more independent depth decides which to follow (METHODS_3D 4.4)
3 Navionics app 52.483189, -4.054940 (30, 245) (beach salient edge); 52.484802, -4.055772 (-150, 300); 52.481658, -4.055733 (200, 300) drying heights / depths at these three points (all near the LAT water line) units and datum checks the chart datum (LAT assumed): the LiDAR has the water edge at -2.3 mODN near y 245 m
4 Google Earth Pro (historical imagery) 52.483539, -4.056951 (-10, 381) head edge; 52.483996, -4.055334 (-60, 271) tail the date of the imagery with the LOWEST water at the reef (springs, around the equinoxes; 2018-2025), and a screenshot of both mounds on that date; ruler distance from the defence line (52.483475, -4.051330) to the head edge image date; ruler in metres the rock above -2.3 mODN is surveyed (LiDAR); a lower-tide photo would show the toe berm and flanks that the model takes from the design (A11)
5 Google Earth Pro 52.483538, -4.057231 (-10, 400) elevation / depth readout (if the layer shows bathymetry) at the cursor, and the date of the imagery m, datum as stated by GE rough depth seaward of the reef head (Fig 2 -4.0 contour is at y 410-450 m)
6 UKHO EasyTide / Admiralty Tide Tables Vol. 1 (Aberystwyth, UK) about 52.41, -4.09 (Aberystwyth harbour; pick the port in the app) HAT, MHWS, MHWN, MLWN, MLWS and Z0 (mean level above chart datum), in m above chart datum metres above chart datum closes the HAT gap (slider currently stops at MHWS) and the +-0.15 m MSL offset (MSL = +0.31 mODN estimated; LAT = -2.44 mODN from neighbouring ports)
7 Any (drawing set) - drawing 9V5090/1023 S1-S1 dimensions the oval 23,000 + 23,000 mm between SOP R15 and R14 (46 m) but the setting-out table of drawing 1020 puts them 38 m apart; if you have the CAD or the contractor's as-built, which is right? m oval flat-top length (about 2 % of the oval volume)

Optional, if you have it: a post-2022 drone or boat sounding of the reef, or the Phase 1 as-built drawings (Ceredigion County Council or the contractor), which would replace the design bed level (about -4.0 mODN) that now limits the model.

versions.name: Laser survey edge (Welsh Government LiDAR, 19 Mar 2022)
versions.method: 1 m LiDAR DSM (lightly smoothed, sigma 0.8 m) inside the exposed-rock outline; below the water edge the Royal Haskoning toe-berm slopes (1:1.5), 2 m flat blanket and 1:1.5 blanket edge (drawings 1021-1023) down to the modelled seabed.
versions.level: rock exposed at the water level during the flight (about -2.3 mODN)
versions.note: Default (Lior 2026-10-06: laser survey or rock layer are more accurate than a photo). DSM sees block tops, about 0.1-0.3 m above the design surface.

versions.name: Design rock-layer foot (Royal Haskoning drawing 9V5090/1020 rev C1, Jan 2011)
versions.method: Design surface lofted from the crest outline (setting-out points R1-R15, crest levels +0.50 / +1.00 / +0.00 ramp / +1.50) down to the armour foot ring at -2.15 mODN, then the toe berm (1.35 m, 1:1.5), 2 m blanket apron and blanket edge rings of drawing 1020, onto the modelled seabed.
versions.level: foot of the Type 4 armour layer = top of the toe berm (about -2.15 mODN)
versions.note: The as-designed rock layer; the as-built flanks are flatter and 8-10 m wider than the design (LiDAR).

versions.name: Visible rock edge (Esri satellite photo, 17 Sep 2024)
versions.method: Traced rock edge (79 vertices) as the footprint; LiDAR DSM inside; design toe slopes below the edge (assumed 1:1.5 from the edge down to the bed, i.e. steeper than the real flanks).
versions.level: bare rock above the waterline in the photo (about -1.3 mODN from the DSM at the traced edge)
versions.note: Smallest footprint: the photo shows only the rock above the water at that tide, so it understates the structure; kept as the traceable photo outline.

models.versions_info: Three outlines of the same two rock mounds. Default: the laser-survey edge (Welsh Government LiDAR, flown 19 March 2022 at about the lowest spring tide): the rock exposed at water level, 8,675 m2, built from the LiDAR surface plus the design toe slopes (a measured surface is more accurate than a photo). Second: the design rock-layer foot of Royal Haskoning drawing 9V5090/1020 (Jan 2011), 6,989 m2. Third: the visible rock edge in the Esri photo of 17 Sep 2024, 5,743 m2, the outline that was traced first and is kept for traceability. Areas differ because the three edges sit at different heights on the same sloping flanks, not because the structure moved.

models.name: Boscombe Surf Reef
models.state_short: As built, finished September-October 2009: idealised two-layer loft of the traced outline (2011-09-28 image) at the design crest +0.5 m ACD. The damaged April 2011 survey surface is an evidence layer only.
models.state_full: AS-BUILT 2009 (intact, finished Sept-Oct 2009): idealised loft of the verified outline with the design crest +0.5 m ACD. Evidence layer: April 2011 DGPS surface (after the container failure).
models.caption: AS-BUILT 2009 state (intact reef). Later: containers failed from March-April 2011 (one 70 m bag lost ~80 t of sand, 2 m crest dip), closed 31 Mar 2011, repairs never completed, ASR liquidated Sept 2012, site re-branded for diving/snorkelling 2014/2017; the bags still lie on the seabed in damaged form and still show as a shoal on the Navionics chart. Not modelled as a second state.

confidence.reason: Outline (2011 satellite), seabed (April 2011 DGPS plot, +-0.2 m colour read) and the as-built crest (designers +0.5 m ACD, Oct 2009 survey +0.45..0.65) are all sourced and agree, and Garmin Navionics shows the same shoal; but the zero of the survey plot (chart datum) is assumed (+-1.4 m if wrong), the as-built flanks and flat crest are an idealised loft, and the ground under the reef and the strip between the beach profiles and the survey (y ~35-100 m) are interpolated. From 2026-10-07 the beach is a measured profile (Channel Coastal Observatory, April 2010) and it also supports the chart-datum reading (CCO minus model = +0.03 m, sd 0.30 m); the seabed beyond y = 380 m is an EMODnet-slope extrapolation, flat alongshore since D2 2026-10-10 (+-0.5 m).
confidence.reason_short: Outline (2011 satellite), seabed (April 2011 DGPS plot) and the as-built crest (designers +0.5 m ACD; Oct 2009 profiles) are sourced and agree, and Navionics shows the same shoal; but the survey zero (chart datum) is assumed (+-1.4 m on absolute heights if wrong) and the flanks and flat crest are an idealised loft.

Survey date 2010-04-20 = nearest date at which all 11 lines near the reef exist (2009-09-22 / 2009-11-30 exist on 1-2 lines only)
provenance.uncertainty: +-0.1 m survey; +-0.3 m between survey dates (rms of 2011-03 minus 2010-04 over 11 lines = 0.28 m); +-5 m position (OSGB -> frame); +-0.1 m ODN = MSL; alongshore interpolation between lines 40-60 m apart

provenance.method: Z = base spline seabed + R, R = offset (CCO - base) at the seaward end of each profile line, interpolated alongshore and decaying to 0 over 40 m (smoothstep); cells with survey or under-reef code are never changed
provenance.uncertainty: +-0.5 m (no data between y ~35 and 100 m except the spline)

provenance.method: z_CCO(x_l, y_end) - z_model(x_l, y_end), y_end = last measured point of each line (y 21..38 m), model value = spline extrapolation 65-80 m beyond the plotted survey edge. Independent of EMODnet and Navionics: supports A3 (chart datum) and shows the extrapolation is good to ~0.3 m here

provenance.value: y = 0; model beach surface there z = -0.17 m MSL (range -0.25..-0.09 over x)
provenance.method: surf line of the 2011-09-28 image between px (1300,772) and (1750,720); tide state at that moment unknown. With the CCO beach the surface at y = 0 is about -0.2 m ODN (~MLWN -0.23 m): the line is NOT the MSL waterline (MSL contour lies ~8 m landward, y about -8) and moves with the tide; the viewer also draws the waterline of the selected level
provenance.uncertainty: +-5 m (georeference); tide state unknown

provenance.value: x axis = bearing 83.4 deg, y axis = 173.4 deg
provenance.method: shape.json geo.shoreline_bearing_deg 83.4 from the georeferenced image (north-up Web-Mercator)
both after the April 2011 container failure; repairs began Aug 2011 inside the envelope (shape.json)
provenance.uncertainty: bag-field changes between April and Sept 2011 not resolved

provenance.value: AS-BUILT 2009, intact (idealised loft of the verified outline; crest +0.5 m ACD)
provenance.method: Lior's rule (2026-10-05): model the as-built state; later damage is NOT a second state. Loft: crest = design +0.5 m ACD (Oct 2009 DGPS crest +0.45..+0.65 m, Rendle & Davidson Fig. 9 lower panels), flanks 1:3 from the outline placed on the 1 m relief contour. The April 2011 survey surface (post-damage) is kept only as an evidence layer
provenance.uncertainty: crest +-0.3 m (design +0.5 vs Oct 2009 profile tops +0.05..+0.65, typical +0.2..+0.3), flank +-30%, flat crest idealised (design had a 'focus' and a 'wedge' section whose heights are not published)

provenance.value: drying patch 378 m2 (SonarChart) / 492 m2 (Nautical) vs survey >0 m ACD 296 m2; 0.5 m contour 950 vs 956 m2; 1 m contour 1630 vs 1609 m2
provenance.method: Colour fills of the Garmin Navionics screenshots (green drying, blue < 1 m) converted to canonical metres; compared with the zones of the April 2011 survey surface. Navionics shows the structure as it is now (damaged, not removed). Agreement at 0.5 and 1 m is within 1-2 %, so the same datum (chart datum) is very probable; it may also mean both come from the same survey (the viewer gives no survey date)
provenance.uncertainty: area +-10 % (pixel read, 0.38 m/px); datum of Navionics not stated; independence from Fig. 9 not proven

provenance.value: 16 soundings: mean difference model - Navionics +0.06 m, sd 0.49 m (in the survey area n=4: +0.41 m; extrapolated area n=12: -0.05 m)
provenance.method: 27 spot soundings + 6 contour labels of the Nautical Chart (z17) read by eye (scripts/navionics_reads.json), pixel -> lat/lon -> canonical; model seabed (ACD) sampled at the same point
provenance.uncertainty: read +-0.05 m (printed to 0.1 m) and +-1 m in position; Navionics data date unknown

provenance.value: semi-diurnal with double high water; MHWS-MLWS 1.76 m, max spring range 1.96 m
provenance.method: Water level slider LAT..HAT uses the six Table-1 levels (Bournemouth Pier gauge); heights above chart datum converted with z_MSL = z_ACD - 1.40. The double high water (stand) is not modelled: the slider is a static level, not a time series
provenance.uncertainty: +-0.05 m (table precision); actual level also moves by surge (+-0.5 m) and wave set-up

provenance.value: z(y) = mean over x of z_model(x, 380) - 0.0141 (y - 380), flat alongshore (D2, 2026-10-10); z(x=0, y=650) = -11.58 m MSL
provenance.method: EMODnet DTM 2024 slope -1.41 % (+-0.10 %) from the four full cells beyond the model grid, applied from the alongshore MEAN of the model's own y = 380 row (D2, 2026-10-10: the row and everything seaward of it is flat alongshore; before D2 the spline row was copied column by column and carried a tilt of +0.76 m per 100 m of x that neither EMODnet nor Navionics show); EXTRAPOLATED, no local data. Ties to EMODnet cell means within 0.7-1.3 m (model shallower): y 380: model -7.78 vs EMODnet -8.51 (+0.73); y 445: model -8.69 vs EMODnet -9.98 (+1.29); y 505: model -9.54 vs EMODnet -10.56 (+1.02); y 605: model -10.95 vs EMODnet -11.63 (+0.68)
provenance.uncertainty: +-0.5 m (D2: Navionics z16 check of 11 soundings, rms 0.5 m after flattening; before D2 +-1.2 m with a misfit of about -1.2 m per 100 m of x; REPORT 9.1 had +-1.0 m); EMODnet absolute levels themselves carry +-1.5 m datum/sampling uncertainty at Boscombe

provenance.parameter: EMODnet cross-check of the model seabed (validation, not a model value)
provenance.value: reef-centre cell (ki34288/kj32794, n = 12): EMODnet -5.62 m LAT = -7.08 m MSL; model minus EMODnet = +1.39 m; seven cells fully inside the grid: mean +1.80 m, sd 0.66 m (range +1.14 .. +3.05)
provenance.method: EMODnet cell means vs the model averaged over the same cell footprints (z_LAT = z_MSL + 1.46); not a constant offset (smallest where best sampled), so not a datum shift (REPORT 6.2); the DTM shows no reef; EMODnet is not used for the reef, toe, beach or the seabed around the reef
provenance.uncertainty: +-1.5 m datum and sampling (REPORT 6.2)

caveats.q: Volume
caveats.model: 13,119 m3 (idealised loft)
caveats.stated: about 13,000 m3 (Mead et al. 2010)
caveats.reason: Agreement, within the parameter ranges (slope 1:2 / 1:3 / 1:4 gives 14,184 / 13,119 / 12,161 m3). The April 2011 survey relief (9,573 m3) is the damaged state; the design relief of Fig. 3a gives 11,540 m3.
ev: loft 13,119 m3 against about 13,000 m3 stated (+0.9 %)

caveats.q: Vertical datum of the Fig. 9 survey (the weakest link)
caveats.model: survey zero = chart datum (ACD); z_MSL = z_ACD - 1.40
caveats.stated: Rendle & Davidson p.8: 'MSL is equivalent to Chart Datum, Newlyn' (garbled; not used)
caveats.diff: +-1.4 m on every absolute height if the zero were Ordnance Datum (relief unchanged)
caveats.reason: The authors do not state the datum. Evidence for ACD: crest +0.05..+0.65 m vs design +0.5 m ACD; '2.7 to 5 m depth'; upper section exposed at low springs; EMODnet closer to ACD than to ODN. The viewer has an alternative-datum switch.
caveats.resolve: Rendle PhD thesis (Plymouth), CCO survey metadata, or the Navionics app datum setting
ev: **A3** The depth axis of Fig. 9 is referred to chart datum (ACD).

caveats.q: Seabed depth vs EMODnet DTM 2024
caveats.model: Fig. 9 + spline seabed (April 2011 DGPS)
caveats.stated: EMODnet minus model = -1.8 +- 0.7 m (7 cells; reef-centre cell -1.39 m, n = 12 cells -1.14 / -1.39 / -1.30 m)
caveats.diff: EMODnet 1.8 +- 0.7 m deeper (not a constant shift)
caveats.reason: Cells (116 x 73 m) are larger than the reef; shallow-limit sampling bias of the source survey (CDI 117452) or a datum labelled LAT but effectively ODN (then the difference is +0.18 m for the n = 12 cells). The DTM does not show the reef. EMODnet carries about +-1.5 m of datum and sampling uncertainty and does not override Fig. 9 + Navionics.
caveats.resolve: Vertical datum of CDI 117452 (EMODnet CDI page); a finer UK survey (CCO, UK Civil Hydrography Programme)
ev: -1.8 +- 0.7 m over 7 cells
EMODnet absolute levels at Boscombe carry about +-1.5 m of datum and sampling uncertainty

caveats.q: Plan area
caveats.stated: literature 'about 1 ha'
caveats.reason: The traced outline of the bag field (2011-09-28 image) agrees with two other plan-view sources; 1 ha would need only 1.3 m mean thickness, which does not fit two layers of 1-5 m containers.
ev: The text "about 1 ha" would need 1.3 m of mean thickness

caveats.q: As-built crest height
caveats.model: flat +0.5 m ACD along the whole outline
caveats.stated: Oct 2009 profile tops +0.05 to +0.65 m ACD (typically +0.2 to +0.3); April 2011 maximum +0.68 m; unverified snippet: final crest 0.5 m above the final design height
caveats.diff: +-0.3 m (up to +0.5 m if the unverified snippet is right)
caveats.reason: The 'focus' and 'wedge' sections have different design heights and are not published; settlement 0.5 m or less; the model is an idealised flat crest.
caveats.resolve: Oct 2009 survey grid, Rendle thesis, CCO data request
ev: The final crest height of Boscombe ASR was 0.5 m higher than the final design height

caveats.q: Present-day shoal (Garmin Navionics) vs survey
caveats.model: April 2011 survey zones: drying 296 m2, <0.5 m 956 m2, <1 m 1,609 m2
caveats.stated: SonarChart 378 / 950 / 1,630 m2; Nautical Chart 492 / - / 2,073 m2
caveats.diff: within 1-2 % at the 0.5 m and 1 m levels; drying patch +82 to +196 m2
caveats.reason: Navionics shows the damaged but still present structure; the SonarChart keeps older chart data for drying areas, so it is not fully independent of the survey; chart datum not stated by the app.
caveats.resolve: Navionics app datum / tap on the drying area
ev: 16 soundings on seabed inside the model grid

caveats.q: Offshore seabed (y 380-650 m): alongshore tilt (D2 applied)
caveats.model: row y = 380 and everything seaward flat alongshore (alongshore mean -7.78 m MSL, EMODnet cross-shore gradient 0.0141); r.m.s. 0.51 m against 11 Navionics soundings (was 1.20 m)
caveats.stated: Before D2: EMODnet DTM 2024: no alongshore gradient; Navionics soundings: model -1.2 m per 100 m of x too deep at x < 0 and too shallow at x > 0 (up to +-1.7 m)
caveats.diff: r.m.s. 1.20 m before, 0.51 m after D2 (2026-10-10)
caveats.reason: Before D2 the extension copied the spline row y = 380 (tilt +0.76 m per 100 m of x) to y = 650. D2 flattened it. The zone is context for the shoreline and does not touch the reef or the survey cells. The step between rows 378 and 380 at the x edges is 1.13 m; the 11 hand-read soundings still show -0.44 m per 100 m of x.
caveats.resolve: Applied 2026-10-10 (D2); reversible with 3d/archive/pre_D2/.
ev: Since D2 (2026-10-10) row y = 380 and all rows seaward are set to the alongshore mean

caveats.q: Beach and shoreline date
caveats.model: beach = CCO profile surface of 2010-04-20 (11 lines, m ODN taken as m MSL); viewer draws the waterline of the selected level plus the 2011-09-28 surf line y = 0 (z -0.2 m)
caveats.stated: the traced image is of 2011-09-28 (tide state unknown); beach variability date to date 0.1-0.5 m
caveats.diff: a level error of 0.35 m moves a waterline by about 9 m
caveats.reason: The CCO survey after completion and before the 2011 failure is the nearest date with all 11 lines; ODN is taken as MSL within +-0.1 m (A4).
caveats.resolve: A beach date nearer to autumn 2009 exists on 2 lines only; ask Lior if another date is wanted.

models.methods_html:
METHODS_3D - Boscombe Surf Reef (Bournemouth, UK): three-dimensional model

Note date: 2026-10-05; seabed extension (sections 3.4, 4 items 9-13, 7) added 2026-10-07. Offshore alongshore flattening D2 applied 2026-10-10 (block D2 in 3.4, validation 12, A16, sections 5 and 7). Model files: model.js, index.html, build_3d.py (regenerates model.js and docs.js). Frame, units and datums are defined in section 3.1. Every number below has a source line in SOURCES_3D.md.

1. Summary

The model shows the as-built state of the Boscombe geotextile surf reef (finished September-October 2009): the verified plan outline (4,042 m2, traced on the Esri Wayback image of 28 September 2011, which still shows the bag field clearly) lofted into a two-layer mound with a flat crest at the designers' +0.5 m above chart datum (ACD), 1:3 flanks, standing on a seabed read from the April 2011 DGPS bathymetry plot of Rendle and Davidson (2012, Fig. 9). Later events (container failure from March-April 2011, closure on 31 March 2011, aborted repairs, ASR liquidation in 2012, re-branding for diving in 2014 and 2017) are in the viewer caption and in section 3.10, not modelled as a second state. Garmin Navionics (accessed 2026-10-05) still shows the structure as a shoal with a 380-490 m2 drying patch at the right place, so the bags are damaged but not removed; its shoal areas match the April 2011 survey zones to 1-2 % at the 0.5 m and 1 m levels and 16 spot soundings agree with the model seabed to a mean difference of +0.06 m (sd 0.49 m). Confidence (3D): medium: outline, seabed and crest are sourced and mutually consistent, but the zero of the survey plot is assumed to be chart datum (the whole absolute height scale would shift by 1.4 m if it were Ordnance Datum, relief would not), the as-built flanks and flat crest are an idealised loft, and the beach and the ground under the reef are interpolated or extrapolated. Revision of 2026-10-07: the seabed grid was enlarged from y 0-380 m to y -66 to 650 m (x -160 to 160 m) so that the shoreline is inside the model: the beach and nearshore (y -66 to about +40 m) come from 11 Channel Coastal Observatory beach-profile lines surveyed on 2010-04-20 (S13), the offshore rows (y 380-650 m) extend the model along the EMODnet DTM 2024 seabed slope (S5), and a blend joins the beach to the Fig. 9 survey. The reef, the survey cells and the cells under the reef are unchanged; the new zones are coloured and labelled by source in the viewer (section 3.4).

3. Methods

3.1 Coordinate frame and conversions

The model frame is the canonical frame of shape.json: metres, x alongshore (true bearing 83.4 deg, towards the east; Boscombe Pier is at negative x), y offshore (bearing 173.4 deg, the shore normal), z up. The origin is the point on the surf line of the 2011-09-28 image nearest to the reef centroid (50.719552 N, 1.839278 W; OSGB36 E 411442 N 91115). Heights are metres above mean sea level (MSL), z = 0 at MSL. The three.js scene uses X = x, Y = z, Z = y (right-handed, not mirrored).

(E1) Compass bearing of a canonical direction (dx, dy): bearing = 83.4 deg + atan2(dy, dx). True north in the frame is the unit vector (cos 83.4, cos 173.4) = (0.115, -0.993), i.e. north points mostly towards the beach (-y).

(E2) Image pixel (px, py) of S1 to canonical metres, with s = 0.37808 m/px (Web-Mercator ground scale at 50.72 N, 156543.034 cos(phi) / 2^18), origin pixel O = (1509.7, 747.8), alongshore unit u = (cos a, sin a), a = -6.59 deg, offshore unit n = (-u_y, u_x): x = s [(px - 1509.7) u_x + (py - 747.8) u_y], y = s [(px - 1509.7) n_x + (py - 747.8) n_y]. The 25 traced vertices are reproduced by the fitted 2 x 2 matrix to 0.006 m (the shared tool geom.py had a rotation bug, not used).

(E3) Web-Mercator: X = R lambda, Y = R ln tan(pi/4 + phi/2), R = 6,378,137 m; pixel = (X - X0)/(X1 - X0) W, using the bounds in the .geo.json sidecar of S1.

(E4) Fig. 9 pixel (Xp, Yp) of the left map to OSGB36 metres (gridlines read on the figure: E 411400 at Xp = 147.3, E 411550 at 433.5; N 91000 at Yp = 39.0, N 90820 at 235.3): E = 411400 + (Xp - 147.3)/1.908, N = 91000 - (Yp - 39.0)/1.0909; OSGB36 (EPSG:27700) to WGS84 with pyproj (Helmert, about +-5 m), then E3 and E2 to canonical metres.

(E5) Fig. 9 colour to height: the printed colour bar has ticks 0 to -5 m at bar rows 55, 93, 131, 168, 206, 244 px; the linear fit is z_survey = -0.02646 Y_bar + 1.455 (top +0.93 m, bottom -5.30 m). Each map pixel takes the value of the nearest bar colour (Euclidean RGB distance; median distance 11.7, 95th percentile 20 on a 0-441 scale); pixels whose distance exceeds 70 are rejected. Pixels hidden by the black section line on the left map are taken from the right map (the same surface, offset +469 px, -1 px by template match, SQDIFF 0.028), the rest inpainted (TELEA, r = 4 px). The colour bar saturates at +0.93 m, so crest peaks above it are not resolved.

3.2 Datums and tide levels

(E6) Chart datum (CD) at Bournemouth is 1.40 m below Ordnance Datum Newlyn (S4): z_ACD = z_ODN + 1.40. With ODN approximately equal to MSL (A4): z_MSL = z_ACD - 1.40. Depth below chart datum d_CD = -z_ACD; depth below LAT d_LAT = -(z_ACD - z_LAT,ACD) = -z_ACD - 0.06.

(E7) Water levels (S3 Table 1, converted with E6; model frame, metres above MSL): HAT +1.19, MHWS +0.81, MHWN +0.27, MSL 0 (estimated, A4), MLWN -0.23, MLWS -0.95, LAT -1.46. Check: MHWS - MLWS = 2.21 - 0.45 = 1.76 m, equal to the "1.76 m" printed in the text of S3; the mean of the four mean levels is 1.375 m ACD, consistent with the 1.40 m offset.

(E8) Cover over the design crest (+0.5 m ACD) at level k: c_k = L_k,ACD - 0.50: HAT 2.09 m, MHWS 1.71, MHWN 1.17, MLWN 0.67, MLWS -0.05 (dry), LAT -0.56 (dry). This agrees with S6, which says the upper section is exposed at low spring tides.

The tide at the site is semi-diurnal with a small range and a double high water (a stand around high water; S3 Fig. 1b "highly asymmetrical tide signal"; S11). The viewer uses a static level (slider LAT to HAT, buttons for each datum) and does not model the time curve, wave set-up or surge. Level source: Bournemouth Pier gauge, about 1.5 km west of the reef (S3).

3.3 Plan outline

The outline is the verified polygon of shape.json (S7): the outer edge of the dark bag field on S1, 25 vertices, area 4,042 m2. Its nearest edge lies 181 m, centroid 226 m and far edge 276 m offshore of the surf line (A1, A10). The model draws it as the toe line (magenta) and as the plan of the loft.

3.4 Seabed

The Fig. 9 grid (E4, E5) is resampled to a 1 m canonical grid by bilinear interpolation (no registration shift: a +-30 m search of the best overlap between the survey relief and the outline gives 0, 0 with IoU 0.90), normalised-convolved with a Gaussian of sigma 1 m, with the rim of the plot eroded by 2 cells. The plotted area is 23,500 m2 (y about 100 to 305 m).

The ambient (pre-reef) seabed S(x, y) is a thin-plate spline through the survey cells outside a reef mask (relief above a second-order polynomial > 0.5 m, plus the outline, dilated 5 m; cells decimated to a 6 m spacing; rim buffer 3 m): (E9) S(p) = a0 + a1 x + a2 y + sum_i w_i |p - p_i|^2 ln|p - p_i| (Duchon 1977; scipy.interpolate.RBFInterpolator, kernel thin_plate_spline, smoothing 2.0; Virtanen et al. 2020); the fit r.m.s. on the survey cells is 0.021 m. Inside the survey S = w S_survey + (1 - w) S_TPS with w = clip((d_rim - 2)/8, 0, 1); under the reef S = S_TPS plus the nearest ring residual decayed as exp(-d/8 m) (A8); outside the survey S = S_TPS (extrapolation, A10). The survey-derived grid (E9) is 161 x 191 cells at 2 m (x -160 to 160, y 0 to 380), z in cm, with a code per cell: 0 survey, 1 extrapolated, 2 interpolated under the reef. Until 2026-10-07 this was the whole seabed and its beach cells (y < 100) were spline extrapolation, so the shoreline lay outside the model; the extension below replaces that part.

Seabed extension (revision of 2026-10-07). Lior asked for a larger model in which the shoreline is visible. The seabed grid is now 161 x 359 cells at 2 m (x -160 to 160, y -66 to 650 m; z in cm, one code and one datum weight per cell). Original cells keep their values wherever they carry code 0 or 2 (checked cell by cell against the previous model.js: 0 of 4,295 survey cells and 0 of 1,580 under-reef cells changed; the reef grid, reef statistics, Navionics layer, water levels and the datum switch are identical to the 2026-10-05 build). The new or changed cells carry three further codes:

(E13) Beach rows, y = -66 ... -2 m (code 3). The CCO points (E, N, z_ODN) of each of the 11 lines l are converted from OSGB36 to the canonical frame with the chain used for Fig. 9 (OSGB36 to WGS84 with pyproj, then the S1 pixel grid, +-5 m), giving x_l(y) and z_l(y) (points with equal y averaged, clamped beyond the first and last point). At a row y the surface is the piecewise-linear interpolation across the lines ordered by x, constant beyond the outer lines: z(x, y) = interp_x(x; {x_l(y)}, {z_l(y)}). The lines are nearly shore-normal (x_l drifts by at most about 6 m over y -60 to +20 m), so interpolation at constant y is adequate. Seven lines lie inside the 320 m grid (x -142 to +145 m); 428A (x -183 m) and 424A (+176 m) lie just outside and fix the edge columns by interpolation; 429 and 424 (x -221 and +222 m) lie further out and are not needed for the grid.

(E14) Transition rows, y = 0 ... 380 m, only cells that were code 1 (no survey, not under the reef). With S the thin-plate spline of E9: z(x, y) = S(x, y) + R(x, y), R = interp_x(x; {x_l(y)}, {r_l(y)}), where r_l(y) = z_l(y) - S(x_l(y), y) for y <= y_end,l (the seaward end of line l, y = 21-38 m; code 3 there) and r_l(y) = delta_l (1 - sm((y - y_end,l)/L)) beyond it (code 4 while the blend weight exceeds 0.02), with delta_l = z_l(y_end,l) - S(x_l, y_end,l), sm(t) = t^2 (3 - 2t) clipped to [0, 1] and L = 40 m. The offsets delta_l are the data of the datum test (validation 9) and are small (mean +0.03 m, sd 0.30 m), so the join is nearly seamless.

(E15) Offshore rows, y = 382 ... 650 m (code 5). z(x, y) = z380 - s (y - 380) with z380 the alongshore mean of the model row y = 380 (since D2, 2026-10-10; before D2 it was the column value z(x, 380)), s = 0.0141 m/m (+-0.0010), the mean seabed slope of the four complete EMODnet DTM 2024 cells at y about 380, 445-505 and 605 m (cell means -7.05, -8.52 to -9.10 and -10.17 m LAT; project test REPORT 9.1). Only the slope is taken from EMODnet, not its levels: its cell means are 1.1 to 3.1 m deeper than the survey seabed and the DTM does not show the reef, so the absolute level continues from the model's own row y = 380 (alongshore mean -7.78 m MSL; the EMODnet cell at y 380 is -7.05 m LAT = -8.51 m MSL with z_MSL = z_LAT - 1.46, i.e. the model is 0.7 m shallower, inside the +-1.5 m datum/sampling uncertainty of EMODnet here). Row y = 380 is itself a spline extrapolation (the survey ends at y about 312 m) and had an alongshore slope of +0.76 m per 100 m of x which E15 copied to y = 650 m before D2; validation 12 showed that this was the main error of zone 5. Since D2 (2026-10-10) row y = 380 and all rows seaward are set to the alongshore mean (block D2 in 3.4); stated uncertainty of zone 5 now +-0.5 m.

(E16) Datums of the extension. CCO heights are m ODN; the model zero is MSL and ODN = MSL within +-0.1 m (A4), so z_MSL = z_ODN on the beach. Survey-derived cells keep E6, z_MSL = z_ACD - 1.40. The viewer's alternative reading "survey zero = ODN" adds 1.40 dw to the survey-derived cells, with the datum weight dw = 0 on the CCO beach (referenced to ODN independently of Fig. 9), dw = 1 - W in the blend (W the blend weight) and dw = 1 on survey, spline and zone 5 cells.

Shoreline. The waterline of a level is the contour of z at that level on this grid; the viewer draws it for the selected level and keeps the 2011-09-28 surf line y = 0 as a separate line. With the CCO beach (slope about 0.04 between +1.2 and -0.3 m) the waterlines lie at y = -3 to -8 m (MSL), -10 to -30 m (MHWS), -27 to -37 m (HAT), +24 to +38 m (MLWS) and +51 to +72 m (LAT, in the blend zone), depending on x; the surf line y = 0 stands at z = -0.2 m (about MLWN). A level error of 0.35 m (section 5) moves a waterline by about 9 m. The model beach is the surface of 2010-04-20, after the reef was finished and before the 2011 container failure; it is not the beach of the date of any image used elsewhere (A14).

D2 (2026-10-10) - offshore row y = 380 and seaward flattened alongshore.

Cause. The extension (E15) copied the model row y = 380 column by column to y = 650 m. That row is a thin-plate-spline extrapolation of the Fig. 9 survey (which ends at y about 312 m) and carries an alongshore slope of +0.76 m per 100 m of x (-8.94 m at x = -160 to -6.79 m at x = +160, range 2.15 m). 3.5 Reef surface (as-built, default)

(E10) Idealised loft: r(x, y) = clip(r0 + phi/m, 0, H_c), H_c = max(z_c - S, 0), z_reef = S + r, with phi the signed distance to the outline (positive inside, metres), r0 = 1.0 m (the outline is placed on the 1 m relief contour of the survey, which gives IoU 0.90 with the satellite outline), m = 3.0 (run per rise, A7) and the crest z_c = +0.5 m ACD (the BUILT crest, Rendle 2016 p. 70; design 0 m CD, Rendle Table 4.4, or 0.3 m CD, Fig. 5.3 drawing; A6). The flat crest plateau covers 1,780 m2; the mean relief inside the outline is 3.2 m. Volume V = sum r dx dy = 13,119 m3 against about 13,000 m3 stated (S3).

(E11) Evidence layer (not a reef state): the April 2011 survey surface z_surv = S + max(Z_s - S, 0) inside the reef mask, available through the "Reef surface" selector. It shows the container failure (offshore half of the axis at -0.8 to -2.8 m ACD, S2 profile: a 2 m crest dip and a trough of -1.1 to -2.2 m) and supplies the shoal-area comparisons in section 4.

3.6 Garmin Navionics reading (S9)

The old ChartViewer is gone; the Garmin Marine Maps page (title "Garmin | Marine Maps", footer "Not to be used for navigation") serves the Navionics Nautical Chart and SonarChart layers without login or CAPTCHA, and was used in an own headless Chrome (private profile, not the shared browser pane). Settings: chart type Nautical Charts or SonarChart Maps, depth units metres, shallow shading 1 m (blue = shallower than 1 m; SonarChart splits it into 0-0.5 m dark blue and 0.5-1 m light blue; green = drying, above chart datum). The Google Places search box gave no suggestions in headless mode, so the map was centred on 50.71753 N, 1.83891 W with the page's own Leaflet setView at zoom 16, 17 and 18 (18 is the maximum). Pixel to ground (E12): mercator metres per pixel 156543.034 / 2^z, pane 1000 x 751 px at screenshot offset (400, 113), centre (500, 375.5); validated against Leaflet's own latLngToContainerPoint to 0.5 px. Areas are pixel counts times (0.378 m)^2 at zoom 18; outlines come from skimage.measure.find_contours; positions go through E3 and E2 to canonical metres. Thirty-three soundings and contour labels printed on the chart (a digit with a subscript is metres and tenths) were read by eye from 3x enlarged crops (scripts/navionics_reads.json); position reading accuracy about 1 m.

Is the structure "ruined" for the Navionics rule? The bags were damaged (S2: one 70 m container lost about 80 t of sand in April 2011, an adjacent one lost by 2012; S12: repairs never completed, debris on the beach in 2017) but not removed: the 2025 Esri image shows a blurred patch with the same envelope (METHOD.md), and Navionics today shows a distinct shoal with a green drying patch at the shoreward-east half of the old bag field (centroid canonical (15, 209), 12.7 m from the survey crest zone). The offshore half is no longer distinguishable from the sloping seabed. Decision: the structure still exists and is recognisable, so Navionics is used for the seabed and as a cross-check of the shoal and the post-damage crest, but it does not set the as-built crest (that comes from the designers and the Oct 2009 profiles) because it shows the damaged state.

3.7 Viewer rendering

Seabed and reef are triangulated heightfields coloured by depth (seabed) or relief (reef). The water surface is a translucent plane at the chosen level L. Vertical exaggeration e (1 to 5, default 1, always displayed) scales all heights, including the water level and the datum labels: z_shown = e z, so the apparent flank gradient is tan(theta') = e tan(theta) (a 1:3 flank, 18.4 deg, looks like 33.7 deg at e = 2 and 59 deg at e = 5); distances in plan are never exaggerated. The photo-match mode forces e = 1. The survey-datum switch (A3 alternative) lifts the surveyed seabed and the April 2011 surface by 1.40 m against the water; the as-built crest is NOT lifted (the designers state it in chart datum, +0.5 m ACD = -0.90 m MSL), so under the switch the loft is rebuilt on the raised seabed, the relief shrinks by up to 1.4 m, the crest ends up under water at MSL, and the survey no longer matches the Navionics shoal lines (which are drawn in chart datum and never move). Camera parameters follow: heading as E1, pitch positive up, roll, vertical field of view, horizontal hfov = 2 atan(tan(vfov/2) aspect), 35 mm equivalent focal length f = 18 mm / tan(hfov/2).

3.8 Assumptions

  • A1 The outline traced on S1 (28 Sep 2011) is the as-built outer envelope; the envelope did not change between 2009 and 2011 (S7: same footprint in the 2025 image; the loss of containers lowered crest heights, not the footprint).
  • A2 Fig. 9 is a faithful, smooth rendering of the DGPS surfaces: features finer than 3-5 m are not trustworthy; heights are read to +-0.2 m.
  • A3 The depth axis of Fig. 9 is referred to chart datum (ACD). Evidence: crest in the Oct 2009 profiles +0.05 to +0.65 m against the designers' +0.5 m ACD; "225 m offshore in 2.7 to 5 m depth" and "3-5 m (CD)" match the survey seabed -3 to -5 m; S6: upper section exposed at low springs; EMODnet is 1.3-1.7 m deeper than the survey read as ACD but 3 m deeper if read as ODN; Navionics shoal areas match without a shift. The text of S2 ("MSL is equivalent to Chart Datum, Newlyn") is garbled and is not used. A switch in the viewer shows the alternative (survey zero = ODN).
  • A4 MSL = ODN within +-0.1 m at Bournemouth (S8: usual range centred +0.02 m ODN), so MSL is 1.40 +-0.1 m above chart datum.
  • A5 The Bournemouth Pier tide levels (S3 Table 1) apply at the reef 1.5 km east.

5. Uncertainty

Propagation (independent errors, first order): sigma_f^2 = sum_i (df/dx_i)^2 sigma_i^2.

  • Crest in the model frame (E6): z_crest,MSL = h_c - D, sigma^2 = sigma_hc^2 + sigma_D^2, with sigma_hc = 0.3 m (A6), sigma_D = 0.1 m (A4): sigma = 0.32 m. Crest below LAT: d_LAT = -(h_c - z_LAT), so the crest stands 0.56 m above LAT (d_LAT = -0.56 m), sigma^2 = sigma_hc^2 + sigma_LAT^2, sigma_LAT = 0.05 m (table precision): sigma = 0.30 m.
  • Reef height at a point: H = z_c - S, sigma_H^2 = sigma_hc^2 + sigma_read^2 + sigma_tps^2, with colour read 0.2 m and interpolation under the reef 0.3 m (TPS ring r.m.s. 0.02 m, but the pre-reef seabed is unobserved): sigma_H = 0.47 m on a mean height of 3.2 m (median surveyed relief 2.3 m, maximum 4.1 m, after damage and smoothing). The datum risk is separate: if the survey zero were ODN, S would be 1.4 m higher in the model frame and H smaller by 1.4 m (absolute heights of the survey shift, relief of the survey does not).
  • Beach and nearshore (zone 3, E13): sigma^2 = sigma_date^2 + sigma_D^2 + (sigma_pos tan(beta))^2 with sigma_date = 0.28 m (validation 10), sigma_D = 0.1 m (ODN = MSL, A4) and the position error 5 m on a slope tan(beta) = 0.04 (0.2 m): sigma = 0.36 m. A waterline at a given level is displaced by sigma / tan(beta) = about 9 m. Blend zone (code 4): 0.5 m (A15). Offshore zone 5: 0.5 m since D2 (validation 12; it was 1.2 m before D2), correlated along x.
  • Seabed depth at a point inside the survey: sigma = 0.2 m (colour read) plus the plot's own interpolation; extrapolated: 0.5 m from the Navionics comparison (validation 6), growing with distance.
  • Volume: (sigma_V/V)^2 = (sigma_A/A)^2 + (sigma_H/H)^2 + (sigma_m)^2, with area +-5 % (1 m outline error on a 120 x 45 m field), height 0.47/3.2 = 15 %, slope 5 %: about 16 % (the sensitivity runs in validation 2 span -12 % to +14 %).
  • Outline: +-1 m on the west, east and south edges, +-1.1 m on the shoreward edge (S7); position of the whole frame relative to the true geography about +-5 m (Esri georeference, OSGB conversion).
  • Navionics: area +-10 % (pixel read, boundary smoothing), soundings +-0.05 m read, +-1 m in position.
  • Vertical exaggeration: affects only the picture. At e = 3 a height error of 0.3 m looks like 0.9 m; slopes, crest cover and volume look larger by e. Use e = 1 for any quantitative reading and for photo matching.

6. Confidence

Level: medium. Against the rubric: the plan shape is itself rated medium (area 60 % below a repeated "about 1 ha" in the literature, three plan-view sources agree with each other); the seabed is read from a real DGPS plot (+-0.2 m) and confirmed by 16 independent Navionics soundings (mean difference +0.06 m); the as-built crest is given by the designers and checked against the Oct 2009 profiles (+-0.3 m); tide levels come from a gauge table in the design paper and the datum offset from the national tide facility. What keeps it from "high": the zero of the survey plot is an assumption (A3), strongly supported but not stated by the authors (the text is garbled); the as-built flanks and the flat crest are idealised (A6, A7; the two-level "focus" and "wedge" sections of the design are not published); the beach and the pre-reef seabed under the reef are interpolated (A8, A10); no as-built survey grid exists in the sources, only profiles of October 2009.

Datum of the Fig 9 survey (the weakest link) - reasoning, 2026-10-05

  • Rendle 2012 p.8 says "In the UK, mean sea level (MSL) is equivalent to Chart Datum, Newlyn ... (0 m contour in Fig. 10)" - garbled (chart datum is NOT MSL); it concerns the beach 0 m contour, and could mean Ordnance Datum Newlyn (CCO beach surveys use ODN).
  • Evidence the reef survey depth axis is Chart Datum: (1) the 2009 crest in Fig 9 is +0.4 .. +0.8 and the designers' crest is +0.5 m ACD (a 1.4 m ODN offset would put the crest 1.4 m above the design); (2) Rendle p.3 "225 m offshore in 2.7 to 5 m depth" and Mead "water depths of 3-5 m (CD)" match the survey seabed at the reef (-3 .. -5); (3) Herbert 2017: upper section exposed on low SPRING tides = crest +0.5..+0.8 ACD, not +1.9 ACD; (4) EMODnet (LAT) is deeper than the survey by about 1.5 m, not 3 m (check below).
  • Decision: survey datum = Chart Datum (ACD). The viewer keeps an "alternative datum" switch (survey zero = ODN ~ MSL) so the effect of being wrong can be seen. Flagged in provenance as estimated, uncertainty +-1.4 m (all absolute heights; relief unaffected).

Survey (April 2011, as ACD): y 100-200 about -1.4..-2.5; y 220-300 about -3 .. -4.8. EMODnet is deeper by 1.3-1.7 m (older / smoothed, pre-nourishment data probable), which is closer to the CD reading than to ODN (3 m). Only used as a datum plausibility check, not for values.

REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR - Boscombe Surf Reef 3D model (2026-10-05)

The model is built and usable as it is (confidence medium). The items below are what I could NOT read myself, or only partly. Each one says what I assumed meanwhile, so nothing is waiting on you. Coordinates are decimal degrees, WGS84 (lat, lon); I computed them from the verified outline and the model frame (x alongshore, y offshore, see METHODS_3D.md 3.1).

What I did read myself (so you do not need to repeat it): the Garmin Navionics web viewer (Nautical Chart and SonarChart, metres, zoom 18) - the old ChartViewer is gone, but maps.garmin.com/en-US/marine shows both layers without login; soundings and shoal areas are in annotated\navionics_*.png. The viewer does NOT state a depth datum or a survey date, and it prints no drying height.

A. Navionics app (phone / tablet), SonarChart or Nautical Chart, depths in metres

Tool Exact lat/lon (or place) What to read Datum / units to note Why it matters for the model
Navionics app 50.717704, -1.838728 (centre of the green drying patch) tap the green patch: drying height or depth at point; repeat at 3 other points inside the green patch (about 5 m apart) metres; write down any datum line the app shows (chart datum / LAT?) and whether tide correction is ON the web viewer prints no drying height: this gives the present crest height above chart datum (model crest as built: +0.5 m ACD; survey April 2011 peak +0.68 m)
Navionics app 50.717851, -1.838682 (peak of the April 2011 survey) depth at point metres tests whether the shoal peak of the chart is the same as the survey peak (13 m away from the green patch centre in my reading)

models.name: Bunbury Airwave
models.model_name: Bunbury Airwave: sand-slurry-ballasted rubber (Hypalon) bladder, as installed Dec 2019 - torn, not a working reef
models.state_short: As installed, December 2019: 12 m sand-slurry bladder, torn along a glued seam before completion (card verdict FAILED). Geometry only; it never operated as a reef. Removal, redesign and the 2025 granite proposal are not modelled.
models.state_full: Installed bladder (installation attempted December 2019: began the week of 9 Dec, seam tear spotted Fri 13 Dec at about 90 % complete), torn before completion - not a working reef
models.caption: Installed bladder (December 2019: install week of 9 Dec, seam tear spotted Fri 13 Dec), torn before completion - not a working reef. Card verdict: FAILED. Sand-slurry-ballasted Hypalon rubber, removed within days; no independent record of rideable waves. The developer's "In 2018" is contradicted by every dated 2019 report (Methods 2.1; this model uses December 2019). Shape drawn = symmetric-cap stand-in.

confidence.reason: MEDIUM, by the rubric in METHODS_3D.md section 6. The seabed comes from an airborne-lidar survey of this exact beach (smooth 1:24 slope), an independent Navionics chart agrees with it to 0.32 m RMS once its depths are read below LAT, and the tides are from a port table. The text-implied seabed (crest 1 m below low tide + 1.6-2 m height) is reached by the lidar at y = 42-50 m, inside the 30-50 m text range. Against that: the survey is from 2009, its 10 m cells cannot resolve the 12 m reef, the offshore distance is a 30-50 m text range (+-0.4 m of depth), and the crest depth, height and flank shape are text or estimates. Crest depth below MLLW is 0.69 +- 0.66 m (Monte Carlo over the position and height ranges), against 'about 1 m' in the text. The as-installed bladder was partly filled, unanchored and torn, so its true surface differs from the symmetric cap drawn.
confidence.reason_short: Seabed (2009 lidar, cross-checked by Navionics, RMS 0.32 m) and tides are sourced; reef height, crest depth and the installed shape are text-based or assumed, and the bladder never operated.

models.methods_html:
METHODS_3D - Bunbury Airwave (Bunbury Back Beach, Western Australia): three-dimensional model

Built 2026-10-10 by build_3d.py (numbers in this note are filled in by that script from shape.json, the reef card, data/lidar_*, and data/nav_transects.json; edit METHODS_3D.template.md, not this file). Companion notes: SOURCES_3D.md (running log of what was read where), REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR.md (what could not be read), annotated/ (the sources with the readings marked: lidar figures and N1-N4 for Navionics).

1. Summary

The model shows the Bunbury Airwave as installed in December 2019: a 12 m diameter bladder of Hypalon (synthetic) rubber with glued seams, partly filled with sand slurry (washed beach sand, 140-150 t by the developer's own figures), water and air, lying on the nearshore seabed of Back Beach, 30-50 m off the waterline, with the water surface at any tidal plane from LAT to HAT. It is not a rock reef and not a working reef: the installation began in the week of 9 December 2019, a diver spotted a tear along a glued seam on Friday 13 December when the bladder was about 90 % complete and not fully anchored, and it was removed within about three days. The card verdict is FAILED and stays so; the developer's page says "In 2018" and "wasn't a failure", but the year is contradicted by every dated 2019 report and no independent source documents rideable waves (section 2.1). The seabed is the WA Department of Transport airborne-lidar survey of 2009 (10 m grid), cross-checked against Garmin Navionics SonarChart contours I counted from the web viewer (RMS 0.32 m once its depths are read below LAT, the Australian chart datum); tides are the Port of Bunbury planes (GHD 2021). The footprint is the verified circle of shape.json; the height (1.6-2.0 m), crest depth ("about 1 m" at low tide) and profile are text-based, and the surface drawn is a symmetric spherical-cap stand-in because no cross-section of the installed bladder exists. Later events (removal, redesign, the 2025 granite proposal) are not modelled; they are in the viewer caption and in section 2.1. The 3D confidence is MEDIUM: the seabed and tides are sourced and independently cross-checked, but the reef geometry is text-based, the crest depth below MLLW is 0.69 +- 0.66 m (Monte Carlo over the position and height ranges) against "about 1 m" in the text, and the real bladder was partly filled and torn.

2.1 Chronology of the structure: what state is modelled, what is not, and why December 2019

Dates are as the card records them (year: "Installation attempted December 2019 (failed during install); concept development began ~2008-2009 [R2]"). The date check below is the one in the card's developer_account table (5 claims checked on 2026-10-05).

date event in the model? source (card refs)
2018-08 Waveco's crowd-funding campaign (Kickstarter) fails; nothing deployed. The only 2018 events found. no (caption/methods only) R3, R19
2019-06-13 ABC: the Airwave is set to be installed in November 2019. no (caption/methods only) R2
2019-08-12 Tracks: first live trial planned for mid-November at about 45 m offshore; the crowd-funding was 'last year'. no (caption/methods only) R23
2019-10-14 Raised Water Research: construction half-way. no (caption/methods only) R4
2019-11-15 Tracks: 12 m diameter, 1.6 m tall at the highest point; live trial 'in the next couple of months'. no (caption/methods only) R9
2019-12-07 to 12-13 Installation week (from Mon 9 Dec): slurry pump and hoses on the beach (7 Dec, forum observer); three divers and a boat. no (caption/methods only) R9, R15, R1
2019-12-13 (Fri) A diver spots the tear along a glued seam: bladder about 90 % complete, not fully anchored. THIS INSTALLED, TORN STATE IS WHAT THE MODEL SHOWS (geometry only). yes (geometry) R1, R5, R7, R15
2019-12-16 (Mon) Tear reported (ABC, RWR, The Inertia, SurferToday). Bottegal: unexpected deep swell and undertow. no (caption/methods only) R1, R5, R6, R7
within about 3 days Bladder removed from the water (reports range from about 5 hours to 3 days). no (caption/methods only) R8, R18, R15
2020-07-09 Second prototype planned for December 2020 (about A$300,000 more needed); not confirmed built. no (caption/methods only) R18
2021-10-08 Tracks: Bottegal 'readily admits' the first trial was a failure; sand pumped too heavily into one quadrant; redesign with welded compound, only tank-tested. no (caption/methods only) R22
2022-03-22 Bunbury Mail: Bottegal says 'not a failure'; glued Hypalon seams; a lone 0.75 m wave seen (developer's account only); back in the water 'by Summer 2024'. no (caption/methods only) R8
2025 Waveco's Bunbury proposal is a granite (rock) reef, not the rubber Airwave. The About page (last modified 2025-12-22) says 'In 2018 ... successfully created peeling waves ... wasn't a failure' (year contradicted, waves not independently supported). no (caption/methods only) R20, R21

Waveco's "2018" versus the record. The developer's page says: "In 2018, we deployed a 150-tonne sand-slurry bladder at Bunbury’s Back Beach. While it successfully created peeling waves, a final-day overpressure event led to a seam split. It wasn't a failure—it was the catalyst for our next breakthrough." (Waveco 2025; the passage is undated; the page was created 2019-08-11 and last modified 2025-12-22). The independent record places the installation in December 2019: ABC (2019a) said on 13 June 2019 that it would be installed in November; Tracks (2019a) on 12 August 2019 described a trial planned for mid-November and a crowd-funding campaign "last year"; Raised Water Research (2019a) said on 14 October 2019 that construction was half-way; Tracks (2019b) on 15 November said the live trial would be "in the next couple of months"; and then ABC (2019b), Raised Water Research (2019b) and The Inertia (2019) reported the tear on 16 December 2019, with a forum observer (Swellnet 2019) describing a slurry pump and hoses on the beach on 7 December and the bladder "partially filled" on 13 December. The only 2018 events are a failed Kickstarter and a "may be installed" preview (SurferToday 2018). One outlier, the 2022 Bunbury Mail intro ("four years since", a supplied photo captioned 2018), conflicts with every dated 2019 report. This model therefore uses December 2019 (installation week of 9 December, tear spotted Friday 13 December), not 2018. The geometry does not depend on the date, but the label does.

Waveco claim (2025) independent record (card) assessment
"In 2018, we deployed" December 2019, see above contradicted
"a 150-tonne sand-slurry bladder" sand slurry corroborated (Tracks 2019b, Bunbury Mail 2022, RWR, forum observer); mass developer-only, 140-150 t type consistent; mass unverified
"successfully created peeling waves" no independent report, photo or video of surfable waves; at most one 0.75 m wave, reported by the developer 27 months later; nobody rode it not independently supported
"a final-day overpressure event led to a seam split" seam split confirmed; "overpressure" matches his 2021-22 explanations, not his 2019 one (deep swell and undertow); the tear was on about the fifth day, at about 90 % complete partly supported
"It wasn't a failure" Tracks (2021): Bottegal "readily admits" the first trial was a failure; no completed trial; second prototype unconfirmed; 2025 proposal is a granite reef a judgement, not a checkable fact

The card's verdict reason, verbatim: "The structure tore along a glued seam during installation (spotted Fri 13 Dec 2019, about 90% installed and not fully anchored), was removed within days, and never operated as a completed reef [R1][R5][R8][R18]. No independent report, photo or video documents rideable waves on it; the only wave claim is the developer's own later account of one lone 0.75 m wave seen during installation [R8][R21]. The developer's page says the trial 'wasn't a failure' [R21], but it misdates the deployment to 2018 (it was December 2019), Tracks reported in 2021 that Bottegal 'readily admits' the first trial was a failure [R22], no second install is confirmed [R18][R8], and by 2025 Waveco's Bunbury proposal is a different (granite) design [R20]. Verdict kept as 'failed' after checking the developer's account (2026-10-05). Update 2026-10-10: the verdict stays failed, because the structure failed within days (a seam opened) and was never a durable reef. In fairness, the founder (Troy) told Lior the reef worked amazingly, with perfect waves, until the seam opened, and that the final design uses sand instead of air and the next step is concrete [R25, personal communication, notes as reported by Lior]. That is a developer statement and independent confirmation of surfable waves is still lacking." The verdict stays FAILED; no developer claim overrides it (rule of this project).

2.2 Source disagreement: what the bladder was filled with (recorded 2026-10-10, nothing in the model changed)

source statement type
Tracks Magazine (2019b) "sand + air fill": washed, coarse beach sand for the slurry, plus air independent press, relays the developer
ABC News (2019b) the structure is "filled with air" independent press, loose wording
Bunbury Mail (2022); Kennedy (2021); Waveco (2025) sand slurry, 140 t (Bunbury Mail, Kennedy) or 150 t (Waveco) developer's own figures
Bakalo (2026), interview with Troy (S_Troy, card R25) "final design uses sand instead of air; engineers found air did not respond well with the waves" developer, personal communication, unverified

How this documentation treats it: this model describes the December 2019 attempt as a sand-slurry-ballasted bladder (sand slurry, water and air; assumption A14). That agrees with S_Troy on sand and with Tracks (2019b) and Bunbury Mail (2022) on slurry, and it does not claim an air-only fill. What is NOT resolved: whether the December 2019 bladder already had the "final" sand design that Troy describes or was an earlier, partly air-filled version (ABC and Tracks mention air), and whether "final design" means the 2019 attempt or a later, untested version. The reef card lists this under sources_disagree (fill type, failure timing, wave performance, future). Two further differences recorded there: Troy says the seam opened "a couple of days after installation", while the 2019 press (ABC 2019b, RWR 2019b) reports a tear at about 90 % complete, not fully anchored; Troy says the waves were "perfect", for which there is no independent record (the verdict stays FAILED). None of this changes a model value: the surface is a rigid spherical cap and carries no fill (A12).

3. Methods

3.1 Coordinate frame and orientation

The model frame is the canonical frame of shape.json: metres, x alongshore toward bearing 12.32 deg true (NNE), y seaward toward bearing 282.32 deg true (WNW, x turned 90 deg anticlockwise), z up, z = 0 at mean sea level (MSL). (x, y, z) is right-handed; the viewer maps model (x, y, z) to three.js (X, Y, Z) = (x, z, -y), which is mirror-free. The origin O is the foot of the perpendicular from the site point on the fitted 0 m AHD contour of the 2009 lidar (MGA94 zone 50: E 372378.8, N 6311547.1); y = 0 is that contour (about the MSL waterline of 2009).

The contour was fitted to the zero crossings of the lidar along 201 grid rows (|north| <= 500 m): east = a + b north with a = 38.7 m and b = 0.2046 (relative to the site point; rms scatter 8.4 m). With t = (b, 1)/sqrt(1 + b^2) the unit vector along the contour and n = (-t_N, t_E) its seaward normal:

(E, N)_grid = O + x t + y n                                   (E1)
bearing_true = bearing_grid + gamma,   gamma = 0.754 deg   (PROJ, MGA94 zone 50 at the site)   (E2)
north in the model frame = (cos bx, cos by)                   (bx, by = true bearings of +x, +y)    (E3)

Orientation assumption (A1): +y is perpendicular to the 2009 0 m AHD contour. The Navionics 0 m line (green/blue edge) is tilted +2.4 deg against the model x axis (section 4, V9): slightly more than the +-2 deg contour scatter, which is plausible for two lines drawn 10 years apart.

3.2 Vertical datums and conversions

All elevations are held relative to AHD and converted to the model zero with the Port of Bunbury table (GHD 2021, Table 1: MSL = +0.1 m AHD):

z_MSL = z_AHD - (MSL - AHD) = z_AHD - 0.1 m                              (E4)
a depth d below datum D (D given in m relative to AHD):   z_AHD = D - d          (E5)
depth of a point at level L below a plane P (both m AHD):  d(L | P) = P - L        (positive = below)   (E6)
crest depth below plane P:                                  d_c(P) = P - (z_bed + H)                  (E7)

Tidal planes used (m relative to AHD; the model z is that minus 0.1): HAT 0.6, MHHW 0.2, MLHW +0.1, MSL +0.1, MHLW 0.0, MLLW -0.2, LAT -0.6 (LAT is the chart datum since 2009; in m above chart datum 1.3 / 0.9 / 0.7 / 0.7 / 0.6 / 0.5 / 0.1). In model z: HAT 0.5, MHHW 0.1, MHLW -0.1, MSL 0, MLLW -0.3, LAT -0.7 m. The range HAT - LAT is 1.2 m ("maximum tidal range of 1.2 m", "predominantly diurnal", GHD 2021). The DoT survey index gives LAT = AHD - 0.57 m for Bunbury (difference to the table: 0.03 m). The values are rounded to 0.1 m by the source; the gauge is the Bunbury Port inner harbour, assumed valid at Back Beach (A9). "Low tide" in the RWR crest-depth text is not defined; MLLW is assumed (A6) and LAT shown as the alternative (0.4 m lower).

3.3 Plan shape

The toe polygon (29 vertices, 112.1 m2) is read unchanged from shape.json (status verified, verified 2026-10-04, plan confidence medium, md5 f046605f97ddb20b3fb80a86d07b9a03). It is a circle seen at about 27 deg off nadir on the drone photo, rectified by stretching the minor axis; the 12 m scale is the text-stated diameter (so the agreement of 112.1 m2 with pi 6^2 = 113.1 m2, -0.9 %, is by construction). The photo shows a paler crescent on one rim (probably a slumped or damaged quadrant); excluding it would shrink the diameter by about 8 %. The viewer evaluates the outline as a radial function r(theta) about the polygon centre.

3.4 Seabed from the WA DoT 2009 airborne lidar (primary)

The BAG (10 m point grid, MGA94 zone 50, SW cell centre E361415 N6305610) was read once (stage 1, build_3d_lidar.py) and resampled bilinearly into the model frame on a 5 m grid, x = -150 ... +150 m, y = -40 ... +200 m (61 x 49 nodes):

z_AHD(x, y) = bilinear( grid, E1^-1 (x, y) )                                       (E8)

In the surf zone (y about -15 ... 35 m) there is no lidar return; 286 of 2989 nodes (9.6 %) are filled with the alongshore median profile P(y) (linear across the gap) plus a smoothed per-column offset o(x):

z_fill(x, y) = P(y) + o(x),   o(x) = 5-column moving average of median_y[ z(x, y) - P(y) ],  -40 <= y <= 80 m      (E9)

The profile statistics (median, 10th and 90th percentile over |x| <= 100 m, native sampling, 2.5 m in y) give, in m AHD: y = 20 m -1.10, 30 m -2.08, 37.5 m -2.58, 40 m -2.69, 45 m -2.97, 50 m -3.20, 60 m -3.62, 100 m -5.11, 150 m -7.12, 200 m -8.40. The mean slope for y = 30-100 m is 0.0409 (1:24.5), with no bar or trough within 200 m. The MLLW line (-0.2 m AHD) lies at y = 4.1 m, the LAT line (-0.6 m AHD) at 13.9 m and the MSL line at 2.4 m. The viewer meshes the 5 m grid; filled nodes are tinted. Contours (every 1 m AHD) are drawn from the filled grid.

The 12 m reef covers 1-2 native cells, so the seabed beneath it is a sloping plane, not resolved relief (A7). The survey is 10 years older than the installation (A8).

3.5 Reef surface (spherical-cap stand-in)

No cross-section of the installed bladder is published; the sources say "dome" (ABC 2019b), "a very subtle, flattened dome with a steeply angled back" (The Tradie Magazine 2019, seen in search text only), and, for the first bladder, "a bit of a skateboard ramp type thing" (Kennedy 2021). Default surface (A5): a symmetric spherical cap of base radius a = 6.0 m and height H (default 2.0 m, range 1.6-2.0 m, both design figures reported before the install). With R_s the sphere radius and t = r / r_rim(theta) in [0, 1] the normalised radial distance (so that the base follows the traced outline):

R_s = (a^2 + H^2) / (2 H)                                  H = 2.0 m: 10.00 m, H = 1.6 m: 12.05 m          (E10)
cap(t) = sqrt( R_s^2 - (a t)^2 ) - (R_s - H)                                                                       (E11)
z_surface(x, y) = z_bed(x, y) + 0.03 + cap(t)             (the cap follows the sloping bed; 0.03 m seats it)       (E12)
V = pi H (3 a^2 + H^2) / 6                                 H = 2.0 m: 117.3 m3, H = 1.6 m: 92.6 m3     (E13)
rim angle  theta_rim = asin(a / R_s)                       H = 2.0 m: 36.9 deg, H = 1.6 m: 29.9 deg  (E14)

An optional ramp asymmetry A (0-0.6) displaces the apex towards a chosen true bearing (steeper on that side); no source says which side was steep, so the default is symmetric. No fill, valves, hoses, anchors or the tear are drawn (A12). The default centre is y = 37.5 m (shape.json); the viewer presets 30, 37.5, 45, 49.1 m (Tracks: "approximately 45 metres off the low tide mark", i.e. 4.1 + 45) and 50 m (SurferToday 2019).
