3.6 Navionics (Garmin Marine Maps) as an independent seabed check

Access. webapp.navionics.com redirects to Garmin's Marine Maps viewer (https://maps.garmin.com/en-US/marine/). In my own headless Chrome (a fresh temporary profile and a random free DevTools port, never the shared browser pane; the script src/navionics/capture_navionics.py terminates only its own process tree) the page loaded with no login, CAPTCHA or consent dialog; nothing was accepted or bypassed. The page's own key (a geohash of the site) and Leaflet setView centred the map on -33.3276, 115.6284 at zoom 18 (the maximum) and 17, with Chart type = SonarChart Maps (or Nautical Charts), Depth units = Meters, Seabed areas = Hide, Shallow shading 1 m (the metres default). The app states no depth datum and no contour interval. Screenshots (private research copies, "Not to be used for navigation") were analysed offline; they were re-captured after a port-isolation notice and are byte-identical.

Scale and geometry. Web-Mercator: res = 156543.034 cos(lat) / 2^zoom / dpr = 0.2495 m per pixel at zoom 18 with device pixel ratio 2. A model point maps to the image through the true bearings of the model axes (E3).

Counting. 9 shore-normal transects (alongshore offsets -120 ... +120 m, step 30 m) run from the site point along +y. Along each, band boundaries (green drying area, dark blue, light blue, white) and thin dark contour lines were located (runs closer than 2.5 m merged because depth digits cross some lines). Index n = 0 is the green/blue boundary (the 0 m contour), n = 1 the dark/light blue boundary, n = 2 the light blue/white boundary (the 1 m shallow-shading limit), n >= 3 the thin lines. The interval 0.5 m is inferred and checked against the printed labels (1, 1.5, 2, 3, 3.5, 4, 4.5, 5 ... 8.5 on successive lines); every transect has 17-18 lines, monotonic and mutually consistent. The Nautical Charts layer shows contours 0 / 2 / 5 / 10 m and spot soundings, and agrees with the SonarChart lines (2 m at s = 3.1 m and 5 m at 75.1 m from the site on the main transect, against 2.1 and 77.2 m in SonarChart).

Datum test. For the n-th line the depth is d_n = 0.5 n m below the unknown datum D, so the lidar elevation there must equal D - d_n (E5). For a candidate datum D_c the misfit is the RMS of z_lidar(y_n) - (D_c - d_n) over the lines with valid lidar (y >= 30 m, inside the 300 x 240 m grid, not gap-filled); the free-fit datum is the mean of z_lidar + d_n:

candidate datum z (m AHD) RMS, 9 transects (n=111) bias lidar - Navionics RMS, main transect (n=12)
LAT -0.60 0.32 -0.24 0.35
LAT (DoT index) -0.57 0.34 -0.27 0.38
MLLW -0.20 0.67 -0.64 0.73
MHLW +0.00 0.87 -0.84 0.93
AHD +0.00 0.87 -0.84 0.93
MSL +0.10 0.96 -0.94 1.03

The free-fit datum is -0.84 m AHD (sd 0.20 m over lines; standard error 0.019 m if the lines were independent, which they are not). Result: the Navionics depths are below LAT (the Australian chart datum); MSL and AHD are rejected (RMS 0.87-0.96 m), MLLW is disfavoured (RMS 0.67 m, twice that of LAT) but not excluded by the lidar's own 0.48 m uncertainty alone. Independent anchors: the 0 m Navionics contour lies at lidar -0.69 +- 0.19 m AHD (surf-zone strip, indicative; LAT is -0.60, DoT index -0.57); the only Nautical-chart spot sounding inside the lidar grid (3.5 m at x = 106.8, y = 76.0 m, lidar -4.02 m AHD) implies -0.52 m AHD; the 2 m and 5 m Nautical contours imply -0.78 and -0.69 m AHD.

A Monte Carlo check (40000 draws: y uniform 30-50 m, H uniform 1.6-2.0 m, seabed and tide errors Gaussian as above) gives a crest depth below MLLW of 0.69 m with sd 0.66 m (5th-95th percentile -0.41 to 1.78 m); 32 % of draws are at least as deep as the text's 1.0 m. Weighting the draws by the text ("about 1 m", sigma 0.30 m) puts the reef centre at y = 41.2 +- 5.4 m (the viewer's "set offshore so crest = 1 m under MLLW" button solves the same condition). At the default y = 37.5 m, H = 2.0 m the crest is 0.38 m below MLLW, which is 0.9 standard deviations shallower than the text's 1.0 m (combined sigma of E17 and the text): consistent.

So the crest is 0.38 m (H = 2.0) to 0.78 m (H = 1.6) below MLLW at the default position, with sigma_dc = 0.63 m. Below LAT the crest is -0.02 m (H = 2.0: the cap just reaches LAT) to 0.38 m (H = 1.6).

Vertical exaggeration VE multiplies every z (water, seabed, reef) and leaves x and y unchanged: tan(angle_apparent) = VE tan(angle_true); at VE = 5 the 1:24.5 bed looks like 1:4.9 and the 2.0 m cap looks 10.0 m high, with its rim angle 36.9 deg steepening to 75.1 deg. Camera angles read for photo alignment are only valid at VE = 1; the viewer forces VE = 1 in photo-match mode.

6. Confidence

MEDIUM. Rubric used (my extension of the plan-shape rubric in SHAPE_SPEC.md, which covers only the outline): high = built-state footprint from a survey or georeferenced image, crest and seabed from surveys at the site and mutually consistent within 0.3 m, position known to better than 10 m, a measured as-built surface; medium = all vertical inputs sourced and consistent within 0.5 m, with at most one of (the surface shape is assumed, the footprint is a design, position known only to +-50 m); low = two or more of those, or vertical uncertainty at least half the reef height. Against it: the seabed is sourced (lidar) and independently supported (Navionics, RMS 0.32 m below LAT); the tides are sourced and cross-checked (0.03 m); the text-implied seabed and the lidar agree to 0.22-0.62 m at the default position and exactly at y = 42.0-50.0 m, inside the text range; the footprint is a verified outline from a photograph of the installed bladder (plan confidence medium); the offshore position is known to +-10 m (sigma_y 5.8 m). The one assumed element is the surface shape (A5), which makes it MEDIUM rather than HIGH; the height (1.6-2.0 m) and crest depth are text-only and the vertical uncertainty of the crest depth (0.63 m) is below half the reef height (0.8-1.0 m) so it is not LOW. Two cautions keep it from being stronger: the survey is 10 years older than the install and its cells cannot resolve the footprint, and the real bladder was partly filled, unanchored and torn, so the cap drawn is a stand-in for a shape nobody measured. The plan confidence (medium) is separate from this one.

REQUESTS FOR LIOR - Bunbury Airwave (Bunbury Back Beach, WA), 3D model (2026-10-05)

What the model already has: tide planes (GHD 2021, checked against the DoT survey index), seabed (WA DoT 2009 airborne lidar, checked against the Garmin Navionics SonarChart contours I counted myself from the web viewer, RMS 0.32 m once depths are read below LAT), plan outline (verified circle, 12 m), reef height and crest depth (text). The bladder was removed in December 2019, so Navionics shows no structure and was used for the seabed only. What I could NOT read, and could not find anywhere online, is listed here. The model is already built with stated assumptions; each row says what it would change. Neither tool can show the structure itself except Google Earth historical imagery, and only if an image from 9-20 December 2019 exists (the nearest imagery I found at the site is 2016 and 2025).

All coordinates are decimal degrees, WGS84 (lat, lon). They are computed from the model frame (origin -33.32767, 115.62880 = the 2009 0 m AHD contour; +x = 12.3 deg true alongshore, +y = 282.3 deg true seaward). Points are on the model's alongshore line x = 0 through the site point unless stated; a depth reading at them is a valid seabed reading whatever the true reef position is.

A. Where exactly was the bladder? (largest geometric unknown: +-100 m alongshore, +-10 m offshore)

# tool exact lat/lon or place what to read datum / units to note why it matters for the model
A1 Google Earth Pro, historical imagery slider Bunbury Back Beach, centred on -33.3276, 115.6284, 30-50 m seaward of the waterline, just south of the Bunbury SLSC building (-33.3271, 115.6298) the date of every image from Dec 2019 to Jan 2020 (the bladder sat in the water about 9-16 Dec 2019 and was removed within about three days); if one shows the pale circle, drop a placemark on its centre and copy the lat/lon, note the image date and whether the tide looks low WGS84 decimal degrees; image date (day) fixes the position (now a text/satellite estimate, +-100 m alongshore, +-10 m offshore = +-0.4 m of seabed depth)
A2 Google Earth Pro, ruler (path) from the A1 placemark (or, if no image shows it, from -33.3276, 115.6284) to the water's edge in the SAME image, along the shore normal (bearing about 282 deg true) distance in metres and the bearing the ruler shows metres; image date and whether the sand is wet/dry at the edge the distance offshore (text 30-45 m / 45 m from the low-tide mark / 50 m; each 10 m moves the seabed depth by 0.4 m)
A3 Google Earth Pro, ruler from the SLSC building corner (-33.3271, 115.6298) to the A1 placemark distance (m) and compass direction metres; degrees true confirms "just to the south of Bunbury surf club" (Tracks 2019) and the model's alongshore position
A4 Google Earth Pro, historical imagery the point -33.32767, 115.62880 (the model's 2009 0 m AHD contour) in the imagery nearest 2009-2010 and in the 2025 image: ruler distance from this point to the water's edge along bearing 282 deg; the image date and tide state metres; sign (+ seaward) shows whether the 2009 shoreline (which defines y = 0 for every distance in the model) has moved (2025 Esri waterline is about 7 m from the 2009 contour at the site)

B. Seabed depth (cross-check of the 2009 lidar and of my contour counting)

models.name: Mount Maunganui Beach Reef ("Mount Reef")
models.model_name: Mount Maunganui Beach Reef ("Mount Reef"), New Zealand
models.state_short: As built, completed mid-2008: idealised loft of the verified outline (default: the -2.0 m CD contour of the 18 Jul 2013 multibeam survey; version 2: the 2008 as-built toe) on the 2026 Navionics seabed shifted to an ASSUMED as-built bed. The reef was removed in Sep-Nov 2014 and no longer exists.
models.state_full: AS-BUILT reef, completed mid-2008 (geotextile sand-bag delta wing), idealised loft of the verified outline; evidence layer: 18 Jul 2013 multibeam surface
models.caption: AS-BUILT state (reef completed mid-2008), drawn from the 18 Jul 2013 multibeam outline (default) or the 2008 "Installed" toe outline. z = 0 is present mean sea level (MSL = Chart Datum + 1.13 m); the depth datum of the surveys, Chart Datum, and MVD-53 (CD + 0.96 m) are drawn as labelled datum lines. LATER CHANGES (not modelled): by 13 Jul 2013 the apex bags were deflated to -2.0 .. -2.4 m CD and the small north-arm base bags were probably buried; the five-year consent lapsed in 2010; the bags were removed from 25 Sep 2014 to the weekend of 8-9 Nov 2014 (all bags above the seabed, NZ$87,000); fabric washed ashore on 18 Jan 2023. The reef no longer exists. The seabed outside the reef is the Garmin Navionics SonarChart of 2026 (not for navigation) shifted to the selected as-built bed level.

confidence.reason: Plan, crest and tides are sourced: the outline is the -2.0 m contour of the 2013 multibeam survey (confirmed on a second raster and the aerial), the crest -0.9 m CD agrees with the BoPRC text and both survey figures, and the tide levels are LINZ values for Tauranga. The weak links are the as-built bed (ASSUMPTION -3.6 m CD, option -2.8; Lior D1) and therefore the reef height (about 2.7 m at -3.6, 1.9 m at -2.8) and the flank shape: every later source reads the bed 0.8-1.2 m shallower than the assumed -3.6 (0.0-0.9 m for the Oct 2006 read), and the stated 2,800 m3 is only reproduced with a bed of about -3.51 to -3.66 m CD. The seabed outside the reef is the 2026 Navionics SonarChart (datum tested against the 2013 survey), not the 2008 seabed.
confidence.reason_short: MEDIUM: outline, crest and tides sourced; the as-built bed is an ASSUMPTION (-3.6 m CD, reproduces the stated 2,800 m3; option -2.8 for the later seabed), so the reef height (2.7 m, or 1.9 m) is not measured.

caveats.diff: 0.17 m between the two mean-sea-level definitions

models.methods_html:
METHODS_3D - Mount Maunganui Beach Reef ("Mount Reef"), New Zealand: three-dimensional model

Built 2026-10-10 by build_3d.py (numbers in this note are filled in from computed.json, navionics_profile.json, checks.json and ../shape.json; edit METHODS_3D.template.md, not the generated file).

1. Summary

The model shows the as-built reef, completed mid-2008: a delta-wing ("7") of geotextile sand-bag containers off Mount Maunganui main beach (Bay of Plenty), lofted from the verified plan outline with a crest at -0.9 m below Chart Datum (z = -2.03 m relative to present mean sea level) over a seabed taken from the 2026 Garmin Navionics SonarChart and shifted to an as-built bed level of -3.6 m CD, which is an ASSUMPTION (Lior decision D1, 2026-10-07; option "later seabed" -2.8 m CD; sensitivity -3.0 to -4.5). Two outline versions are built: the default, the -2.0 m CD contour of the 18 Jul 2013 multibeam survey (1,071 m2) with a 1:1 skirt to the bed, and the as-built toe outline of the ASR "Installed" survey image (2008, 1,424 m2) lofted through the contour to the crest. Later changes (apex deflation by 2013, buried base bags, removal 25 Sep to 8-9 Nov 2014) are caption and documentation only. Confidence (3D): medium - the outline, crest and tides are sourced; the as-built bed (ASSUMPTION -3.6 m CD) and therefore the 2.7 m height (1.9 m at the option -2.8) and the flank shape are not: every later source reads the bed 0.8-1.2 m shallower than the assumed -3.6, and the stated built volume (2,800 m3) is reproduced only with a bed of -3.51 (survey outline) to -3.66 m CD (toe loft).

2. Data sources and how each was used

Source ids (img1, ctx9, R1 ...) are the ids used in the viewer's "Model data" provenance table and in model.js sources; registry ids (mount-maunganui-reef-img-NN) link to the saved copies and full citations in 03_images/reefs/mount-maunganui-reef/. Page numbers for the BoPRC report are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed page + 1) and were re-checked against the report text on 2026-10-10. Status "used" = feeds a model element; "check" = validation only; "context" = looked at, nothing taken; "rejected" = reason given.

3. Methods

3.1 Frame and datums

  • Canonical metres (shape.json): origin on the wet/dry-sand shoreline nearest the outline centroid (lat -37.6467041, lon 176.2000765); +x alongshore toward true bearing 316.15 deg (NW), +y offshore toward 046.15 deg (NE), z up. (x, y, z-up) is left-handed; the viewer maps (x, y, z) to three.js (X, Y, Z) = (x, z, y), which is right-handed and not mirrored. Compass bearing of a canonical direction (dx, dy): atan2(dx sin BX + dy sin BY, dx cos BX + dy cos BY), BX = 316.15, BY = 46.15; true north in the frame is (0.7206, 0.6934).
  • Georeference chain (explicit, mmr_lib.py): canonical (x, y) <-> NZGD2000 / Bay of Plenty 2000 (EPSG:2106) E, N: (dE, dN) = (x sin ax + y sin oy, x cos ax + y cos oy), ax = 315.99 deg and oy = 45.99 deg grid bearings, origin E0 = 376521.85, N0 = 812664.84; grid convergence -0.161 deg.
  • z = 0 at present mean sea level: z_MSL = z_CD - 1.13 (LINZ Tauranga MSL, 2006-2025 observations). MVD-53 (Moturiki Vertical Datum 1953, the datum of Scarfe 2008 and, assumed, of the ASR image) = CD + 0.9622 m: z_MVD = z_CD - 0.9622 and z_MSL = z_MVD - 0.168; present MSL is 0.17 m above MVD-53. MVD-53 and Chart Datum are drawn as labelled datum lines and on the tide staff.
  • Levels in z_MSL: HAT +1.07, MHWS +0.83, MHWN +0.53, MSL 0, MLWN -0.56, MLWS -0.92, LAT -1.16, MVD-53 -0.168, CD -1.13. Check: spring range 1.75 = 0.83 + 0.92; HAT - MSL = 1.07 vs MSL - LAT = 1.16.

3.2 Reef surface (per outline version)

All reef elevations are computed on a 0.5 m grid (x -44..41, y 277..351) in m CD and converted to MSL; mmr_model.py (Python) and index.html (JavaScript) implement the same rules on the same grids. - Inside the -2.0 m polygons: z = ZC + r(d2) (crest - ZC), ZC = -2.0 m CD, d2 = distance to the polygon edge, r = RISE(d2)/1.10 with RISE = 0 / 0.30 / 0.50 / 0.70 / 0.85 / 0.95 / 1.05 / 1.10 m at d2 = 0 / 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 / 2.5 / 3.0 / 3.5 m (linear interpolation). RISE is the shape of the 2013 DEM (median height above the -2.0 m contour vs distance inside it, west block and south arm: 0.09 / 0.24 / 0.45 / 0.65 / 0.79 / 0.88 / 0.99 / 1.01 / 1.02 m in 0.5 m bins up to 4 m), scaled to the 1.10 m between the contour and the chosen crest -0.9 m CD (A3, A4). Crest options -0.8 / -0.9 / -1.0 m CD. - Default version (survey outline), outside the contour: z = max(S, ZC - dout/run), dout = distance from the -2.0 m region, run = 1 (H:V) (A7). Run is adjustable 0.25-2 in the viewer. - Toe version, between the toe and the contour: z = S + (ZC - S) t, t = dT/(dT + dout), dT = distance inside the union U of the toe and the contour area to its edge (A8). Only 11 m2 of the contour area lies outside the toe, so U = the toe (1,435 m2 vs 1,424 m2). - Reef height h = z - S >= 0 (S = local seabed); volume = sum(h) x 0.25 m2. The reef is idealised: bag-by-bag relief, the scour hole and the 2013 deflation are not modelled.

3.3 Seabed

  • S(y) is alongshore uniform: S(y) = Pnav(y) + (bed - Pnav(y_ref)) x clamp((y - 111.2)/(307.7 - 111.2), 0, 1) in m CD, y_ref = 307.7 m (the reef centroid), Pnav = the Navionics profile of 3.4 (dry beach y < 0: schematic 1:15 ramp, not sourced). Landward of the 1 m contour (y < 111 m) the profile is Navionics as it is; the offset is ramped in towards the reef and kept seaward, so the seaward slope stays the Navionics slope (1:64 at 3-5 m; 1:61 in the 2013 plane fit; BoPRC 1:60-1:110) (A5, A6).
  • Bed level at the reef centre (selector #bed=<id>; scenarios in model.js bed_scenarios, default_bed): -3.6 m CD = ASSUMPTION (default, id assumed) - no source states the 2008-09 bed at the reef; this value reproduces the stated 2,800 m3 and sits inside the evidence range. Option "later seabed" -2.8 m CD (id later) because later surveys read -2.4 to -3.3 m CD. Sensitivity rows -3.0, -3.5, -4.0 (earlier default), -4.5 and "Navionics as it is" = -2.76 m. Evidence for the range: Oct 2006 survey of the unfinished reef (Mead et al. 2007 Fig 12, datum unstated, CD assumed): bed beside the reef 2.0-3.7 m, median about 2.7 m, i.e. shallower than -3.6 (supports the option); reef parts 0.33-1.5 m; Evidence: BoPRC p23 (north-arm side 3.0-4.0 m deep in 2008), ASR Installed ring median -5.4 m MVD-53 = -4.46 m CD (datum assumed), consent depth 3.7-4.6 m, Moores 4.5 m (design); versus 2013 survey -2.4 (NW) to -3.3 m CD (seaward) and Navionics 2026 -2.76 m CD at the centre. BoPRC p29: the bed fluctuates by more than 1 m.

3.4 Navionics reading (seabed only, because the reef was removed in 2014)

  • Garmin's Marine Maps viewer (maps.garmin.com/en-US/marine; the successor of webapp.navionics.com) opened without login, banner or CAPTCHA in an own headless Chrome (random debug port, fresh profile) on 2026-10-06; layers SonarChart Maps (contours every 0.5 m) and Nautical Charts (2 m and 5 m contours only); depth units metres; zoom 17 (0.946 m/px) and 18. The viewer states no datum and no contour interval.
  • With "Shallow shading" = v m the chart paints water shallower than v blue, so the edge of the blue area is the v-m contour (checked against the printed labels). nav_isolines.py extracts the edges (v = 1..10, both layers, both zooms), converts pixels (map centred on the reef centroid, Web Mercator) to canonical metres, and nav_profile.py crosses them with five shore-normal transects x = -100, -50, 0, 50, 100 m. Median y of each contour: 1 m: y = 111, 2 m: y = 242, 3 m: y = 329, 4 m: y = 399, 5 m: y = 463, 6 m: y = 546, 7 m: y = 642, 8 m: y = 728, 9 m: y = 798 (m from the shoreline)
  • Chart depth at the reef centre (y = 307.7) = -2.76 m (interpolated). The 3 m contour bulges 12-17 m seaward at x = 0..50 right at the reef (possible residual of the removed reef; not used). Zoom 18 agrees within 0-6 m. The Nautical layer gives the 2 m contour at y = 266 m and the 5 m contour at y = 489 m (coarser) and one spot sounding 2.4 m at (x 36, y 345), the NE tip of the footprint, where the SonarChart interpolation gives 3.22 m (recorded, not used).
  • Datum test against the 2013 multibeam bed (12,874 one-metre cells of Fig 5 outside the reef and scour-hole zone): reading the chart as CD gives mean difference 0.21 m and RMS 0.30 m (best), as LAT 0.32 m, as MVD-53 0.78 m, as MSL 0.95 m. The chart datum is therefore taken as CD (A5). Figures: annotated/nav_sonar_z17_profile.png, nav_naut_z17_check.png, nav_datum_test.png.

The bottom picture (205 x 211 px) has grid ticks every 26 px on all four edges but no labels, scale bar, north arrow, date or depth legend. Registering our polygons to its bag-top mask (free rotation, scale, mirror) gives the best fit for the mirrored ASR toe outline, IoU 0.87 at 2.5 px/m (grid interval 10.4 m, i.e. 10 m within 4 %); the -2.0 m survey outline fits at IoU 0.69. Bag-top area 1,436 m2 if the grid is 10 m (toe outline 1,424 m2): two independent as-built graphics agree. Mean height implied 2,800 / 1,436 = 1.95 m. Not traced as a new outline version: no labelled scale, date or depth, only 205 px, orientation and position known only through our own polygons, so a trace would reproduce the toe version within +-6 %. It is recorded as corroboration of the toe version (decision on the default: see REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR.md).
  • Mead et al. (2007) Fig 12 top (img-37), Oct 2006 survey of the unfinished reef: 25 depth classes (0.33-5.25 m, positive depths, datum not stated, CD assumed because it matches BoPRC crest -0.8 to -1.0). Reef parts: shallowest class 0.33-0.70, 5th percentile 0.80, median 1.18 m. Bed beside the reef: 10th / 50th / 90th percentile 1.94 / 2.13-2.70 / 3.65 m depending on the ring (deepest class 4.59 m, a pocket west of the reef). Result: bed 2.0-3.7 m, shallower than the assumed -3.6 m; the sand for the bags was pumped from the nearby seabed. Report only; the default was not changed.
  • P3 text, section 4.1.2: the reef was built about 50 m closer to shore than designed (limit of the Port of Tauranga dredge-disposal grounds). This is why the as-built position differs from the design bathymetry (P2 Fig 2); our plan uses the surveyed position (BoPRC Fig 3).
  • P3 text, section 3.1.4: the 6,500 m3 design was "never fully completed"; an adjacent container slumped into the 60 x 6 m gap left by a removed container, leaving a crest about 1 m lower at the offshore end for about 9 months; sand loss from the lower containers; "only 2,800 m3 of the 6,500 m3 design volume currently in place". The model's 2,800 m3 comparison therefore refers to the volume in place in 2011, not to the 2008 completion; BoPRC (2013, p28, citing Mead 2011) and Raised Water Research quote the same figure, so they are one origin, not independent confirmations (A11).

5. Uncertainty

input range effect
crest -0.9 +-0.1 m CD (0.8-1.0 below CD) crest z_MSL = -2.03 +-0.1 m; below LAT 0.87 +-0.1 m; below MLWS 1.11 +-0.1 m
MSL offset +-0.03 m (LINZ MSL 2006-2025); MVD-53 differs by 0.17 m all z shift together
bed at the reef ASSUMPTION -3.6 +-0.5 m CD (option -2.8; range -2.8 to -4.5; 2013 -2.4 to -3.3) reef height H = crest - bed = 2.7 m (1.9 m at -2.8), sigma_H = sqrt(sigma_crest^2 + sigma_bed^2) = sqrt(0.1^2 + 0.5^2) = 0.51 m; volume +-607 m3
flank run 0.25-2 (default 1) survey-version volume 2,567 to 3,421 m3 at the assumed bed -3.6
plan outline +-1-2 m position; lower-bound definition footprint 1,071 to 1,424 m2 (toe) to 1,723 m2 (aerial dark mass)
Navionics profile contour +-2-5 m; datum +-0.3 m seabed away from the reef only; at the reef the bed is the selector value

Vertical exaggeration (1-5x, always shown on screen) stretches heights only: slopes look 1-5x steeper, the plan and the photo-match mode (forced to 1x) are not affected.

6. Confidence

Confidence per element:

element level reason
plan (default) medium measured -2.0 m contour, verified (IoU 0.93 on a second raster, aerial agrees to about 2 m); lower-bound definition, 5 years after completion
plan (toe version) medium-low traced from an undated image without scale bar; scale +-6 %; corroborated by P3 Fig 3 (IoU 0.87)
crest medium-high BoPRC text and two survey figures agree to 0.1 m; 2013 state, "not changed significantly" since 2008 (BoPRC p23)
tides and datums high LINZ and NIWA primary values; MVD-53 offset re-read
seabed shape medium Navionics 2026 with a tested datum; not the 2008 seabed
bed level, height low (ASSUMPTION) no source states the 2008-09 bed at the reef; -3.6 m CD is Lior's D1
volume low-medium follows the bed; the stated 2,800 m3 is a single-origin number (A11)
overall medium see below

Medium. Against the rubric: plan = sourced (verified outline, medium), crest = sourced (BoPRC text and two survey figures agree to 0.1 m), tides = sourced (LINZ primary values), seabed shape = sourced (Navionics, datum tested) but dated 2026; reef height, bed level and flank shape = estimated, with the as-built bed an ASSUMPTION (-3.6 m CD, D1) that is 0.8 m deeper than the later-seabed option (-2.8) and fits the stated volume by construction. Not high because the height - the quantity a surfer cares about - rests on an assumption rather than a measurement; not low because the footprint, crest and datum are individually well supported.

7. Limitations and unknowns

  • The 2008-09 seabed is not known at the reef (the Installed image shows it but its datum is unstated; the 2013 and 2026 sources and the Oct 2006 read are shallower). Mead et al. (2007) and Mead & Borrero (2011) were read: neither gives an as-built plan with scale, a section, a bed or a datum. Lior could supply: the datum of the ASR image (see REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR.md).
  • No section drawing exists; the flank shape is an assumption (steeper than 1:1 is likely); the inner profile is a smooth shape (bags had rounded, grooved tops).
  • The scour hole (to -4.9 m CD in 2013, -6.4 m CD in 2008-09, 7,500 m2) landward in the V is not modelled; the seabed is alongshore uniform.
  • Apex bags are drawn intact at the main crest; the buried base bags of the north arm are in the toe version only.
  • Navionics SonarChart is crowd-sourced and not for navigation; its date is unknown; the viewer states no datum.
  • Google Earth historical imagery 2008-2010 (if the reef is visible) could confirm the as-built footprint; Navionics app depth reads at the reef centre and the 2.4 m sounding would check the web viewer.

8. References

  • Dahm, J. and Gibberd, B. (Focus Resource Management Group) (2013). Mount Maunganui Reef - Assessment of Management Options. Focus Report No. 131, Bay of Plenty Regional Council, December 2013. https://www.boprc.govt.nz/media/558385/mount-maunganui-reef-assessment-of-management-options.pdf
  • Garmin Ltd / Navionics (2026). Marine Maps viewer (SonarChart, Nautical Charts). https://maps.garmin.com/en-US/marine (accessed 2026-10-06; not for navigation).
  • LINZ (2010-11). Bay of Plenty 0.125 m Urban Aerial Photos (2010-2011), CC BY 4.0.
  • LINZ (2026). Standard port tidal levels. https://www.linz.govt.nz/guidance/marine-information/tide-prediction-guidance/standard-port-tidal-levels (accessed 2026-10-06).
  • LINZ (2023). Notes about the Moturiki Annual Mean Sea Level Data. https://www.linz.govt.nz/sites/default/files/data/Moturiki_Readme.pdf
  • Moores, A. (2006). Artificial surf reefs - coming to a beach near you. New Zealand Geographic 78.
  • Mead, S.T., Black, K.P. and Moores, A. (2007). Mount Maunganui Reef - amalgamating design and the constraints of construction. Coasts and Ports 2007, pp 768-773. doi:10.3316/informit.816670201626573.
  • Mead, S.T. and Borrero, J.C. (2011). Multi-Purpose Reefs - A Decade of Applications. Coasts and Ports 2011. doi:10.3316/informit.715072832934166.
  • Bell, R. and Lewis, M. (2006). MHWS level for the Bay of Plenty. NIWA Client Report HAM2006-133 for Environment Bay of Plenty (authors per web search 2026-10-10, not confirmed on the PDF).
  • Raised Water Research. Mount Maunganui artificial reef (ASR "Installed" image). https://raisedwaterresearch.com/spot/artificial-reef/new-zealand/north-island/mount-maunganui/
  • Scarfe, B.E. (2008). Oceanographic considerations for the management and protection of surfing breaks. PhD thesis, University of Waikato. https://hdl.handle.net/10289/2668
  • Balvert, L. (2014). Time called on artificial reef. SunLive, 10 Nov 2014. https://www.sunlive.co.nz/news/86837-time-called-on-artificial-reef.html

  3. [DECISION] Make the as-built toe outline (ASR "Installed", 1,424 m2) the default outline instead of the 2013 multibeam -2.0 m outline (1,071 m2)? Against it: the 2013 survey is a measured survey with a labelled scale. Not applied; the default stays the 2013 survey outline until you decide (asked via main as D8).

  4. [ASK] Datum of the ASR "Mount Reef Installed" bathymetry image (legend -1.8 to -7.4 m). It is read as MVD-53 here; the same reading as CD would move the toe-level ring from -4.46 to -5.4 m CD. A one-line answer from ASR / Raised Water Research settles whether the 2008 seabed was about -4.5 m CD.

  5. [LOOK] Google Earth historical imagery 2008-2010 over -37.6448, 176.2026. If the reef bags are visible (calm, clear day) they confirm the as-built footprint and the north-arm base bags that the 2013 survey no longer shows. Note the imagery date; no download needed.

  6. [LOOK] Navionics phone app: depth at the reef centre and the 2.4 m sounding at about 36 m along the shore and 345 m out. A second reading of the same 2026 SonarChart in the app (with its stated datum) would check the web-viewer reading used for the seabed (-2.76 m CD at the centre).

  7. [LEGAL] Reuse rights of the private research copies before any public release. The BoPRC / Focus RMG report figures, the ASR image, Esri Wayback tiles and Garmin Navionics screenshots are private copies (07_scale/shapes/mount-maunganui-reef/src/ and 3d/src/); none is embedded in the viewer. Only the LINZ aerial (CC BY 4.0) is open-licensed.

caveats.reason: The model shows only the exposed mound seen in the photo and the 2017 multibeam (relief 1-2.5 m); containers are partly buried, stacked, displaced or lost, and the envelope includes gaps.

caveats.q: Crest datum (AHD vs LAT)

models.methods_html:
METHODS_3D - Narrowneck Reef, Gold Coast (Queensland, Australia)

Written 2026-10-10 (stage 2, 3D agent). Reproduce with python prep_multibeam.py, python build_3d.py, python make_annotations.py in this folder. Step log: SOURCES_3D.md. Source audit 2026-10-10 (documentation only, no model value changed): SOURCE_AUDIT_2026-10-10.md in the parent folder; sections 2b, 3.6, 3.7, 3.8 and 6 below were added or extended by it.

1. Summary

The model shows the renewed Narrowneck Reef as left in June 2018 (84 containers added around the 2004-revised structure; about 534 containers placed since 1999). The default plan is the visible container field on the Esri aerial of 8 Aug 2020 (6,239 m2, 7 polygons; a lower bound because the deeper toe is not visible). Four more outlines are selectable (Option 2 renewal design 2017, 2004 revised design, 2011 survey relief zone, Navionics 4.0 m shoals). Heights come from three measured items: the crest (-2.2 m AHD, 2018 multibeam, Vieira da Silva et al. 2021), the 2017 pre-works multibeam of Corbett et al. (2023) Fig 3 (read from its colour scale: seabed -4 m at the shoreward ends of the arms, -7 m at the toe, container relief 1-2 m), and the design contours (crest -2.5 m AHD falling to -6 m). Default outline = the 2020 photo trace: decision D7 by Lior, 2026-10-10 (section 3.8). 3D confidence: MEDIUM (section 6): the plan is a georeferenced photo trace and the heights are measured, but the multibeam is read from a colour picture (+-0.4 m, placed to +-10 m), no post-renewal plan or survey exists, and the crest datum differs by 0.24 m between sources. Reef height is known to about +-1 m; the volumes are mound envelopes (including gaps between containers), not sand-fill volumes.

State and history (not modelled, notes only): 408 containers placed Aug 1999 - Dec 2000 (crest first -1.5 AHD, top-ups to -1.0 LAT in 2001, then lowered to -2.5 AHD); +10 (2002-03), +15 in 2004 (weir and flared wings, the 2004 revised design), +17 (2006); settlement 1-2 m locally (weir containers lowered up to 2 m); renewal 2017-18 with 84 containers (Option 2 layout; the north reef almost fully achieved, the south reef and bridge only partly); crest measured -2.2 m AHD after it. No later change is documented. Sources: Jackson et al. 2007, 2012; Corbett et al. 2023; City of Gold Coast 2020.

3. Methods

3.1 Frame and datums

  • Frame: shape.json canonical (stage 1): origin = waterline of the 8 Aug 2020 image nearest the reef centroid (-27.986800, 153.431127); x alongshore toward bearing 356.21 deg (north), y offshore toward bearing 86.21 deg (east); z up, 0 = MSL; metres.
  • Datum chain (Gold Coast Seaway, MSQ): AHD = LAT + 0.760 m, MSL = LAT + 0.88 m, hence z_MSL = z_AHD - 0.12 = z_LAT - 0.88. Planes above LAT: MLWS 0.22, MLWN 0.51, MSL 0.88, MHWN 1.24, MHWS 1.53, HAT 2.03; with z = 0 at MSL: LAT -0.88, MLWS -0.66, MLWN -0.37, MHWN +0.36, MHWS +0.65, HAT +1.15 m. Local tides only (rule 5); the Snapper Rocks row (MSL 1.09) is not used.
  • Crest datum decision (open issue, 0.24 m). The papers (Jackson 2007 p.7, Corbett 2023 p.3, council layer) write the same design crest as "-1.5 m LAT (RL -2.5 m AHD)", i.e. AHD = LAT + 1.00 m; MSQ gives AHD = LAT + 0.760 m. This model uses MSQ. Reasons: (1) it is the official dated benchmark relation for the nearest standard port, (2) the papers' pairs are rounded, come from one author group and state no derivation, (3) every height here is measured in m AHD (multibeam, Vieira da Silva, design RL), so the choice does not change the geometry; it only moves reef and seabed 0.24 m against LAT/MSL/tide planes. Consequences for the crest: measured -2.2 m AHD = 1.44 m below LAT (MSQ) or 1.20 m (papers); design -2.5 m AHD = 1.74 m (MSQ) or 1.50 m (papers). The viewer has a switch that applies the papers' rule (geometry +0.24 m). Resolution: ask the City or MSQ for the offset used in the 2018 survey.
  • All values were read in AHD; "assumed AHD" is stated where a figure does not name its datum (Corbett Fig 3, Jackson Fig 2). Support: the shallowest container tops of Fig 3 read -1.8 (south arm) and -2.5 m (north arm) vs the measured crest -2.2 m AHD.

3.2 Reef surface

  1. Multibeam raster (Corbett Fig 3, prep_multibeam.py). Scale: the 20 m bar has ticks at x = 274, 295, 317 px: 0.4651 m/px (+-1.2 %); the map is 352 x 312 px = 163.7 x 145.1 m. Depth: the colour bar (x 383-426 px) is fitted linearly through its four tick labels (-1, -4, -6, -9 at y = 140, 198, 253, 305 px; residuals 0.03, -0.23, 0.37, -0.17 m); each map pixel is converted by its hue (the figure is hill-shaded, so brightness is ignored): depth = -0.0472 y + 5.58, hue monotonic from red (-1.7 m) to blue (-7.9 m). Pixels deeper than -7.9 m or paler than -1.7 m are clipped. Bed: grey-scale opening (erosion then dilation, disk radius 10 px = 4.65 m, removes containers narrower than 9 m) and Gaussian smoothing (6 px); relief R = surface - bed (median 0.1 m, p90 0.7 m, p99 1.7 m).
  2. Registration. Assumed north-up with no rotation. Translation chosen by maximum overlap of relief > 0.6 m with the traced 2020 arm polygons (soft mask): image centre at canonical (x -5, y 290) m, +-10 m (the score maximum is broad, 0.52 against 0.51 at 5 m offsets; the south arm fits best; the container field in 2017 differs from 2020 by the 84 added containers). See A1.
  3. Design surface (nn_lib.design_top). Each design (Option 2, 2004) has crest loops (-2.5 m AHD contour) and an outer envelope (-6 m AHD). Inside the envelope the top level is z = -2.5 - 3.5 f, f = d_in / (d_in + d_out) with d_in the distance to the crest loops and d_out the distance to the envelope boundary (1 m raster, Euclidean distance transform). The contours between (-3 ... -5) are NOT digitised; they are replaced by this linear rule (check in 4.2).
  4. Default version (photo). Top = Option 2 design surface lowered to the measured crest (-2.2 m AHD, i.e. +0.3 m), at least 1.0 m above the bed (the containers are visible, so at least one layer; multibeam relief 1-2 m), isolated containers (channel containers, wing patches) 1.8 m above the bed, no top shallower than -1.8 m AHD (the shallowest multibeam value). Footprint = the 7 traced polygons. Side slope: height rises 0.67 m per m inward from the polygon edge (+0.3 m at the edge), i.e. 1.5 H : 1 V (assumption A5).
  5. Design versions. Same rule at the design crest -2.5 m AHD with the Option 2 loops and envelope (version 2), the 2004 loops and envelope (version 3), and the 2004 surface cut to the 2011 relief zone (version 4, an assumption). No minimum height is applied: where the design surface lies below the bed the mound height is zero.
  6. Navionics shoals (version 5): outline only, no solid, because the chart shoals are smoothed (4.0 m over a reef whose crest is -2.2 m AHD = 1.44 m below LAT) and are not a footprint.
  7. Grid. Reef grid 1 m (x -110..110, y 190..420), stored in cm as int16 relative to MSL.

3.3 Seabed

  • Window (about 164 x 145 m around the reef): the opened multibeam bed (3.2), Gaussian 3 m, blended into the surrounding profile over 15 m from the window edge.
  • Alongshore-uniform profile b(y) (PCHIP, nn_lib.seabed_profile), m AHD: window part = median over x of the multibeam bed (y 215-365); seaward Navionics SonarChart labels 7, 8, 9, 10 m read on img-50 at y of about 402, 411, 474, 514 m (map centre = reef centroid +-20 m, 0.4316 m per displayed px, 3.8 deg rotation corrected), converted AHD = -(depth LAT) - 0.76 = -7.76, -8.76, -9.76, -10.76 (LAT assumed; consistent with Vieira da Silva Fig 3 "-9/-10 seaward"), then flat to -11.0 at 540 m; shoreward ASSUMED: 0.0 m at the waterline (y = 0), -1.8 at y = 100 (mean of the Vieira Fig 3 reading -1..-2 and Navionics), -2.1 at y = 190 (the window edge value), +1.2 at y = -40 (beach).
  • Grid 5 m, x -250..250, y -40..520; alongshore constant outside the window (Vieira da Silva Fig 3 shows an alongshore-uniform bed over 1.5 km).
  • Not used: Navionics nearshore contours (its land edge lies about 80 m seaward of our 2020 waterline, so its surf-zone contours are not in our frame); the Navionics "0.9" spot depth (obstruction label, older crest state; Lior's reading is pending).

3.4 Versions and volumes

Volume = sum over the 1 m grid of (reef top - bed) inside the footprint. It is a mound envelope: it includes the gaps between containers and ignores containers buried below the modelled bed, so it is not the sand-fill volume. Bed uncertainty +-0.5 m over the footprint gives the stated +-.

3.5 Water, tides and viewer

Water plane at the selected level (LAT to HAT slider, chips for the MSQ planes and AHD); vertical exaggeration 1-5; datum switch (3.1); other outlines as lines draped on the seabed; faint seaward patches (24 patches, 663 m2, stage 1) as pink lines (not in any outline); photo-match mode (camera position, heading, pitch, FOV; copy camera JSON); presets: oblique from the sea, plan (north = right, shore = top), along the north arm, from the beach at eye height 1.7 m, side view.

3.6 Assumptions

Every one is labelled ASSUMPTION in the place it is used (3.2-3.4, 4.x, the Sources tab provenance 'estimated' flags and the annotated figures). | id | ASSUMPTION | why (evidence) | effect on results (sensitivity) | what would replace it | |---|---|---|---|---| | A1 | Corbett Fig 3 depths are in m AHD | datum not stated; the shallowest container tops of Fig 3 (-1.8 S arm, -2.5 N arm) bracket the measured crest -2.2 m AHD | a different datum would shift the whole window bed: +-0.24 m (MSQ vs papers) shifts reef and bed together; heights above the bed unchanged | the original multibeam grid with its datum (City / ICM) | | A2 | Fig 3 is north-up, rotation 0, scale from the 20 m bar | no north arrow in the crop; relief fits the traced arms | a 3 deg rotation would move the far ends 8 m; registration already +-10 m | original grid | | A3 | Linear colour-bar depth scale through four tick labels | no tick marks on the bar; fit residuals 0.03-0.37 m | depth +-0.4 m everywhere in the window; volume +-23 % (photo) at +-0.5 m | digital multibeam values | | A4 | Design surface between the -2.5 crest loop and the -6 envelope is linear in distance rank (z = -2.5 - 3.5 f) | contours -3..-5 exist in Jackson Fig 2 / Corbett Fig 2 but were not digitised | compared with 53 multibeam blocks: mean offset +0.26 m, sd 0.66 m (4.2); multibeam relief p90 0.9-1.2 m, p99 1.8-2.2 m; no published section | not quantified; only the default (photo) version uses it; affects the flank shape and a part of the volume | photogrammetry or a post-renewal survey | | A6 | Navionics depths are metres below LAT; 3.7 Other methods, tools and AI involvement

  • Scripts that produced numbers (all in this folder or the parent folder; each can be re-run): ../trace_s3.py (trace and shoreline), ../design_registration.py (Fig 7 on s3), ../verify_scripts/ (Option 2 placement, 2004 outline, 2011 zone, faint patches, Navionics loops), prep_multibeam.py (colour to depth, bed), nn_lib.py (design surface, bed profile), build_3d.py (volumes, validation numbers, model.js, docs.js), make_annotations.py.
  • Numerical methods: threshold + morphological closing (plan); normalised cross-correlation and phase correlation (image registration); chamfer fit (Corbett Option 1 on Jackson Fig 2: one isotropic scale, residual 0.65 px); Euclidean distance transform (design surface); grey opening and Gaussian filter (bed); PCHIP interpolation (bed profile); sums over a 1 m grid (volumes). The 5 m seabed grid is bilinear in the viewer.
  • Reading by eye (labelled as such): Navionics labels, Vieira da Silva Fig 3 colours, Jackson Fig 2 contour labels, Corbett tick labels. Each image was viewed once, downscaled.
  • AI: the model was built by Claude agents (stage 1 trace and verification; stage 2 3D; this audit). Their own earlier estimate of reef height (4-6 m at the toe) was checked against the multibeam and NOT supported (4.3); it is not used. Gemini (another AI) supplied nothing that is used: its footprint (two lobes, 400 x 220 m, 75,000 m2) was rejected after we fetched or read the originals (HANDOFF section 9). Re-fetching the Gemini-cited pages was not possible (no network access to the hosts); Black and Mead 2001 is paywalled.

3.8 Decisions log

Who: L = Lior, A = agent, O = orchestrator (main session). | id | decision | options | who / when | reason | |---|---|---|---|---| | D7 | Default outline = the 2020 photo trace (visible container field of 8 Aug 2020, 6,239 m2) | photo trace; Option 2 design (13,941 m2); 2004 design | L, 2026-10-10 (REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR.md 'Decisions taken'); Option 2 stays as a toggle | agent recommendation, which Lior accepted: the photo is the only evidence of the state actually built (no post-renewal survey or drawing exists; Option 2 was built only in part on the south reef). Lior's own wording of the reason is not recorded. Note: the project rule 4 (CLAUDE.md) ranks a survey above a design drawing above a photo trace; no survey of the built state exists and D7 chooses the photo over the Option 2 drawing for this reef | | N1 | State drawn = renewed reef as left in June 2018 | 1999-2000 original; 2004 revised; renewed 2018 | A (stage 1), 2026-10-06 | project rule 5 (latest as-built state); post-renewal imagery shows the containers | | N2 | Primary image = Esri Wayback r9812, 2020-08-08 | 2016, 2019, 2021, 2022-2025, 2025-10 tile sets | A, 2026-10-06 | sharpest image after June 2018 (VERIFY.md, sources.md) | | N3 | Outline = visible container field, not a design contour | design contour; council polygon | A, 2026-10-06 | the design may be 20 m off; the field is what exists; the council polygon is 34,565 m2 (assets envelope) | | N4 | Datum rule = MSQ (AHD = LAT + 0.760) by default, papers' rule (+1.00) as a viewer switch | MSQ; papers; mean of both | A, 2026-10-10 | official dated benchmark; geometry is in AHD so only tide levels move (3.1) | | N5 | Seabed = Corbett Fig 3 multibeam in the window; Navionics only for y 385-540 m | Navionics; Vieira Fig 3 by eye; multibeam | A, 2026-10-10 | measured grid beats chart; Navionics land edge does not match our waterline | | N6 | Navionics '0.9' label and nearshore contours not used | use / not use | A, 2026-10-10 | older crest state or unresolved datum; frame mismatch | | N7 | Design surface by linear rule, contours -3..-5 not digitised | digitise contour by contour | A, 2026-10-10 | checked against 53 multibeam blocks (4.2) | | N8 | Gemini footprint rejected | accept / reject | A, 2026-10-06 | no source supports it | | N9 | Crest not flat: shoreward wedge -2.5 falling seaward | flat crest | A, 2026-10-06 | Jackson 2012 Fig 2 right | | N10 | Navionics 4.0 m shoals: outline only, no solid | solid / outline | A, 2026-10-10 | the chart smooths the reef | | N11 | Local tides only: Gold Coast Seaway, not Snapper Rocks | two gauges | A, per rule 5 | nearest standard port | | N12 | Volumes stated as mound envelopes, not sand-fill volumes | envelope; fill | A, 2026-10-10 | gaps between containers are included, buried containers are not | | N13 | The three E-W shapes in the channel are 'channel containers', not 'weir' | name | A, 2026-10-06 | the 2004 weir containers are N-S and invisible in 2020 | | N14 | Overall confidence MEDIUM | high / medium / low | A, 2026-10-10 | section 6 |

4. Validation

4.1 The five outline versions compared

version (id) date footprint m2 solid mound envelope volume m3 (+- bed 0.5 m) mean / max height m shallowest top m AHD
photo_2020-08-08 (DEFAULT) 2020-08-08 6,239 yes 13,495 (+-3,120) 2.16 / 3.92 -1.8 (arms -2.2)
design_option2_2017 2017 13,941 yes 21,271 (+-6,969) 1.53 / 3.62 -2.5
design_2004_revised 2004 13,631 yes 13,603 (+-6,818) 1.00 / 3.01 -2.3 (bed at the shoreward edge)
survey_2011-06-09 2011-06-09 4,922 yes (assumption A8) 6,856 (+-2,461) 1.39 / 3.01 -2.5
navionics_4.0m_shoals 2026-10-06 537 no none - -
The photo footprint lies 96.6 % inside the Option 2 envelope and 94.5 % inside the 2004 envelope (stage 1). Option 2 holds 1.6 x the 2004 volume because it sits about 22 m further seaward on a deeper bed. The photo volume is a lower bound for the footprint (toe invisible) but an envelope for the material (gaps filled); the two biases have opposite signs, so no net sign is claimed. Decision D7 (default photo vs Option 2): decided by Lior, 2026-10-10: the photo is the default; Option 2 stays a toggle (the only evidence of the state actually built is the photo).

4.2 Design surface vs the 2017 multibeam tops

Blocks of 8 x 8 m inside the 2004 envelope containing relief > 0.8 m (n = 53): the 90th percentile of the multibeam depth per block vs the design surface at the block centre: mean offset +0.26 m (design shallower), sd 0.66 m, correlation 0.76. A positive offset is expected (settlement 1-2 m since 2004); an exponent 0.7 instead of 1 would give +0.02 m (not used: no tuning). Shallowest multibeam tops: north arm -2.51, south arm -1.82 m AHD (p99 -3.13 and -2.72) vs measured crest -2.2 and target -2.5.

4.3 Reef height

Relief above the opened bed: north arm p90 0.92 m, p99 1.81 m; south arm p90 1.22 m, p99 2.22 m (A1 right panel). The stage-1 estimate (2-3 m at the shoreward crest, 4-6 m at the toe) is not supported at the toe: the multibeam bed at the toe is -6.5 to -7.5 m and container tops there -5 to -6, so the relief is 1-1.5 m; at the crest wedge top -2.2 to -3 on bed -4 to -5 gives 2-2.5 m. The opening leaves wide stacks in the bed, so these heights are biased low (the model arms have mean height 2.16 m, maximum 3.9 m at the Option 2 north loop on -6 m bed).

4.4 Seabed and Navionics

Model bed along y (m AHD): 0 at y = 0, -1.8 at 100, -2.1 at 190, -3.9 at 235, -5.1 at 265, -5.8 at 300, -6.8 at 340, -7.3 at 370, -7.7 at 400, -9.6 at 460, -10.5 at 500. Vieira da Silva Fig 3 (A3): inner edge -4/-5 (model -3.9 to -5.1 at y 235-265), under the reef -6 to -8 (model -5.8 to -7.3), seaward -9/-10 (model -9.6 at 460): consistent within +-1 m. Navionics (A2, A5): 4.0-4.5 m LAT over the arms = -4.8 to -5.3 AHD against the model bed -5.1 to -5.8 and crest -2.2 to -4: the chart smooths the reef into a shoal and shows holes of 6 m between; 5.5-6 m around the arms = -6.3 to -6.8 AHD against the model -5 to -6.8 (the multibeam bed is up to 1.5 m shallower); the seaward labels are the data used. Its land edge sits 80 m seaward of our waterline: unresolved; the nearshore profile (A7) remains an assumption.

4.5 Container count vs volume

534 containers x 147 m3 of sand each = 78,500 m3, while the model mound envelope is 13.5k (photo) to 21.3k m3 (Option 2): 17-27 %. Also the footprint of 534 containers (20 x 4 m) would be about 43,000 m2 against 6,239 m2 visible and 13,941 m2 in the design envelope. Containers are therefore buried, stacked below the visible field, displaced or lost: the model shows only what the photo and multibeam show, not the full placed volume.

4.6 Registry rows closed (STEP 0)

img-55 (digitised, A1; results above), img-31 (A3), img-04 and img-01 (A4; same figure), img-50 (A2), img-51 (0.9 label, not used; request to Lior), img-14 (Fig 9 sketch: two layers at the crest; no dimensions), img-24 (drone photo: arms converging seaward and waves peeling from the north arm consistent with the model; no value read). Results are written into 03_images/reefs/narrowneck-gold-coast/images.json (for_3d_check.result).

5. Uncertainty

input range effect
crest level +-0.2 m (no stated accuracy) plus 0.24 m datum ambiguity for LAT values crest depth below LAT: 1.44 (MSQ) or 1.20 m (papers); volume +-0.25 m over the 6,239 m2 gives about +-1,500 m3 (11 %)
bed level in the window +-0.4 m colour reading, +-0.2 m bed estimate reef height +-0.5 m; dV = 0.5 m x area: +-3,120 m3 (23 %) photo
registration of Fig 3 +-10 m local bed and relief shifted, mean levels unchanged to about 0.3 m
design placement +-15 m, scale +-3 % (Option 2) / +-10 % (2004) design volumes +-30 %
bed outside the window +-1 m not part of any volume
vertical exaggeration none on the data; it multiplies all z in the viewer (shown on screen)
Combined reef height at the crest: sqrt(0.25^2 + 0.5^2) = 0.56 m (about +-0.6 m); at the toe +-1 m. Volume (photo): sqrt(3,120^2 + 1,500^2) = +-3.5k m3 plus the footprint lower bound and the gap-filling envelope (not quantified).

6. Confidence

Overall: MEDIUM. Per element: | element | confidence | reason | |---|---|---| | plan (default photo outline) | medium | georeferenced to +-1 m and confirmed on a second tile set (0.2 m) and by Navionics (7-25 m), but only the visible field (lower bound) | | plan (design versions) | medium-low | placed to +-15 m, scale +-3 % / +-10 %, envelopes; Option 2 only partly built | | crest | medium-high | measured -2.2 m AHD (Vieira da Silva 2021), agrees with the multibeam tops (-1.8 / -2.5); no stated accuracy; where it was measured is not stated; 0.24 m datum ambiguity for LAT values | | seabed in the window | medium | multibeam read from a 460 x 312 px colour picture (+-0.4 m, +-10 m, datum assumed) but consistent with Vieira Fig 3 within 1 m | | seabed seaward / nearshore | low-medium / low | chart labels with assumed datum / assumed profile | | reef height and slopes | medium-low | relief 1-2.5 m from the multibeam, biased low; slopes assumed (A5) | | tides | medium-high | official MSQ planes at a port 4 km away; 0.24 m datum link open | | volume | low-medium | envelope (gaps filled) and lower-bound footprint, +-3.5k m3 plus unquantified biases | Against the rubric: the plan is georeferenced and verified (stage 1, medium: visible field only); the crest and the seabed are measured values (2018 and 2017 multibeam), which would be high; but (a) the multibeam is read from a colour figure with an assumed datum, (b) no post-renewal survey or as-built plan exists, (c) the toe below about -6 m is not visible, (d) the nearshore bed and the seabed outside the window are assumed or read from a chart, (e) the datum rule for the tide planes is ambiguous by 0.24 m. Not high because of (a)-(c); not low because crest and bed agree across four independent sources within 1 m.

7. Limitations and unknowns

limitation effect on the model what would resolve it Lior could?
no post-renewal as-built plan or survey footprint = photo field (lower bound); Option 2 south reef only partly built City of Gold Coast renewal drawings / 2018-2019 multibeam; QLD lidar bathymetry 2025 ask the City (e-mail)
Corbett Fig 3 is a 460 x 312 px picture; datum and north not stated bed +-0.4 m, position +-10 m original multibeam grid from ICM / the City ask the City
crest datum offset 0.24 m (MSQ vs papers) crest depth below LAT 1.44 vs 1.20 m the offset used in the 2018 survey (City / MSQ) ask the City
nearshore bed y 0-190 m assumed surf-zone shape between beach and reef Navionics app readings or Google Earth history (REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR.md) yes
Navionics "0.9" label unread an older crest state (1 m below LAT, 2001-2012) app reading at -27.9866, 153.4341 yes

deeper toe invisible footprint lower bound; toe height 1-1.5 m measured only inside the window multibeam of the toe, Option 2 survey no
the 2004 weir containers not visible in 2020 channel mouth shown with 3 small "channel containers" only the City's 2018 survey no

8. References

SOURCES_3D - Narrowneck Reef 3D model: step log

Run started 2026-10-10 (stage 2, fresh agent, Sonnet 5.5). Inputs read: CLAUDE.md, _agent_briefs/common.md + model_3d.md, HANDOFF.md (stage 2 plan, sections 3 and 6), METHOD.md "INPUTS FOR 3D", VERIFY.md steps 6-9. Template: borth-coastal-defence-reef/3d (format only).

CHECKPOINT 0 (2026-10-10) - plan

Frame = shape.json canonical (x alongshore bearing 356.2, y offshore bearing 86.2). z = 0 at MSL. Datum: z_MSL = z_AHD - 0.12 (MSQ). Versions: 5 from shape.json outline_versions, default photo_2020-08-08. Next: STEP 0 image checks (img-55 first), then seabed + reef surface build.

STEP 0 + inputs (2026-10-10)

  • img-55 (Corbett 2023 Fig 3, pre-works multibeam ICM 2017, 460 x 312 px native, map 352 px wide): scale bar ticks at x = 274, 295, 317 px = 0, 10, 20 m -> 0.4651 m/px (+-1.2 %); map covers 163.7 x 145.1 m. Colour bar -1 to -9 (tick labels at y = 140, 198, 253, 305 px; linear fit residuals 0.03, -0.23, 0.37, -0.17 m); depth read by HUE through the bar (prep_multibeam.py). Datum NOT stated; assumed AHD (the shallowest container tops read -1.8 (south arm) and -2.5 (north arm) vs measured crest -2.2 AHD: consistent).
  • Registration of the figure (north-up, rotation 0) onto the traced arms by overlap of relief > 0.6 m: image centre = canonical (x -5, y 290) m, +-10 m (the score peak is broad: 0.52 vs 0.51 at 5 m offsets; the south arm fits best). Annotated: annotated/A1_corbett_fig3_digitised.png.
  • img-31 (Vieira da Silva 2021 Fig 3, survey 1 = 19 Jul 2018, AHD, colour scale -10..8): viewed once; at the MPAR circle the bed is cyan (about -4 to -6), seaward dark blue (-7 to -9); nearshore yellow-green (-1 to -2) within about 100 m of the beach; consistent with the multibeam bed (-4 at the arm ends, -7 at the toe). Annotated: A3.
  • img-04 / img-01 (Jackson 2012 Fig 2): right panel contours -2.50, -3.00, -3.50, -4.00, -4.50, -5.00, -6.00 and outer -8.00 (labelled; datum not printed on the figure); crest wedge -2.50 at the shoreward end of each arm. Used for the surface rule (crest loops + envelope). Annotated: A4.
  • img-50 (Navionics SonarChart z18): contour labels read on the existing overlay (4.0 over arms, 5.5-6 around, 7, 8, 9, 10 seaward; LAT assumed): used for the seaward bed extension y 385-500 (+-15 m) only. The chart's land edge lies about 80 m seaward of the 2020-08-08 waterline in our frame, so its nearshore contours are NOT used. Annotated: A2. img-51 (nautical): spot depths 0.9 and 5.9 only; 0.9 not used (older crest state; Lior's reading pending).
  • img-14 (Fig 9 sketch, T2 on 2 x T4): cross-section sketch, no dimensions; supports "two layers at the crest", not a height. img-24 (drone photo): planform and crest consistent with the model (arms converge seaward, surf peels from the north arm); no number read. img-01: same figure as img-04 (page render).

CHECKPOINT 1 (2026-10-10) - model built

Files: prep_multibeam.py, nn_lib.py, build_3d.py (model.js 0.6 MB, docs.js), index.html (adapted from the Borth viewer: version selector + (i), datum-rule switch, other-outline overlays, photo match), make_previews.py (serves a copy with the vendored three.js; the sandbox cannot reach the CDN). Volumes (mound envelope, m3): photo 13.5k, Option 2 20.9k, 2004 13.8k, 2011 zone 6.9k. Next: annotated images, registry, METHODS_3D.md, docs.js rebuild, HANDOFF/STATUS/REQUESTS.

CHECKPOINT 2 (2026-10-10) - documentation, registry, hand-over

  • annotated/: A1 (Corbett Fig 3 digitised: bar ticks, colour-bar fit, registration, derived bed and relief), A2 (Navionics labels used / not used), A3 (Vieira Fig 3 reading), A4 (Jackson Fig 2 contour labels), A5 (profile: model vs sources), A6 (five versions on the model seabed). Previews: preview_oblique.png, preview_plan.png, preview_methods_panel.png (made by make_previews.py with the vendored three.js, own headless Chrome, random port, fresh profile).
  • Registry (03_images/reefs/narrowneck-gold-coast): pending rows closed (img-01, 04, 14, 24, 31, 50, 51, 55 and img-69 from the papers intake); new rows img-75 (A5), img-76 (A6), img-77 (preview_oblique), img-78 (preview_plan); lines appended to NEW_IMAGES_LOG.md; check_registry.py: Narrowneck passes.
  • img-69 (Blacka et al. 2013 Fig 5.1, surfer standing on the crest in a wave trough): qualitatively consistent with a crest 1.2-1.7 m below LAT; no value read.
  • Navionics y-positions of the seaward labels corrected for the 3.8 deg frame rotation (7 -> y 402, 8 -> 411, 9 -> 474, 10 -> 514 m, +-20 m).
  • Bugs fixed on the way: seabed blend used the array bounds instead of the valid map area (a -5 m dip at y 200 m); viewer AHD read-out under the papers' datum rule.
  • Smoke test (own Chrome): all five versions load, datum switch, other-outline overlay, (i) pop-ups, no console errors.
  • Done. Hand-over: HANDOFF.md top block; 3d/MAIN_TYPED_TEXTS.json.

SOURCE AUDIT (2026-10-10, fresh agent) - documentation only

  • METHODS_3D.md extended: 2b (how each source was used, accuracy, model element; id crosswalk to sources.md), 3.6 assumptions A1-A16 (effect, replacement), 3.7 other methods / AI involvement, 3.8 decisions (D7 by Lior, N1-N14), 6 confidence per element; citations completed (Corbett pp. 663-669 confirmed on the PDF; Vieira da Silva authors; Jackson 2007 Fall 2007; Blacka 2013 full citation); Black & Mead 2001 and the Jackson 2012 DOI listed as not confirmed.
  • build_3d.py: versions_info says D7 decided; confidence text 18 Jul -> 19 Jul 2018 (Vieira da Silva AM p.8 line 176 and p.12 line 312); extra docs keys sources_use_md, assumptions_md, decisions_md (sections cut from METHODS_3D.md); index.html lists them as chips. model.js regenerated: only versions_info and confidence_3d.reason text differ (compared field by field with a build of the previous script); docs.js regenerated.

models.versions_info: Five outlines are stored; the first is the DEFAULT. (1) The renewed reef as it is on the Esri aerial photo of 8 Aug 2020 (the visible container field, 6,239 m2): no post-renewal survey or as-built drawing exists, so the photo is the only evidence of the state actually built; it is a LOWER BOUND because the deeper toe is not visible. (2) Renewal design Option 2 (2017; Corbett et al. 2023 Fig 2): the layout the 2017-18 works followed, drawn to the -6 m AHD contour (13,941 m2); the north reef was almost fully achieved, the south reef and the bridge only partly. (3) The 2004 revised design (13,631 m2): the reef BEFORE the 84 containers of 2017-18. (4) The 2011 survey relief zone (4,922 m2; Jackson et al. 2012): also pre-renewal, no depth legend. (5) Navionics chart shoals shallower than 4.0 m (537 m2): indicative position check only, not a footprint, no solid is drawn. Design outlines are placed to +-15 m and are envelopes larger than the container field. Default = decision D7 by Lior, 2026-10-10 (photo trace; Option 2 stays a toggle).

caveats.reason: With a 1.0 m interval the seaward toe would be at -12.5 m, 5 m below the chart. Absolute depth and height are +-0.5 m; no surveyed depth value was read.
caveats.resolve: As-built multibeam (City of Gold Coast); Navionics app readings A1-A7
ev: With 1.0 m the seaward toe would be at -12.5 m MSL, 5 m below the chart.

models.methods_html:
METHODS_3D - Palm Beach Reef (Gold Coast, Queensland): three-dimensional model

Model files: model.js, index.html, docs.js; regenerated by contours_s7.py, navionics_capture.py, navionics_isolines.py, build_3d.py (which calls write_provenance.py), annotate_3d.py, render_previews.py. All numbers below are read from validation_3d.json (written by build_3d.py). Source log: SOURCES_3D.md. Items the author could not read: REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR.md.

1. Summary

The model shows the Palm Beach artificial reef (a submerged basalt/greenstone rock mound, 162 x 91 m, 11,989 m2 in the model grid, about 225-374 m off the beach at 19th Avenue) as built in May-September 2019; no later works, damage, loss or renewal were found (monitoring papers to 2023 report a stable structure; the rock is visible on Esri imagery of 2025-12-01), so no second state is modelled. The plan outline, the crest outline (59.2 x 5.9 m) and the crest level (-1.5 m below mean sea level) are sourced; the tide planes come from Maritime Safety Queensland. The seabed and the rock surface are inferred: the seabed from the Garmin Navionics SonarChart (read in a headless browser by the author; datum not stated, tested to be LAT), and the rock surface from the 10 unlabelled contour lines drawn on a Nearmap aerial of the finished reef (interval assumed 0.5 m, confirmed independently to within 10 % by the Navionics seabed). The two inferences agree to 0.27 m on average (standard deviation 0.55 m, 427 points) but no surveyed depth value was read. confidence_3d = medium: the geometry is good enough for camera-angle estimation (plan +-1-2 m, crest level +-0.2 m, seabed and reef height +-0.5 m), but the council's asset register (HEIGHT_M 5, VOLUME 33,000) describes a reef 20-33 % larger than the model (crest height 3.9 m, envelope 22,000 m3), and that gap is unresolved.

2. Data sources

Full citations are in section 8. "Resolution" is the practical resolution for this site.

2.1 Chronology and state modelled

Concept design 2013-2015 (DHI; 175 x 144 m, 53,319 m3, offshore toe 560 m from shore in 11.4 m); detailed design (Royal HaskoningDHV) moved the reef about 50 m shoreward and reduced it to 160 x 80 m (Raised Water Research, 2019); construction April/May-September 2019 (Hall/Heron joint venture, 60,000 t, barged from the Port of Brisbane); engineering certification September 2019; later condition "comparable to the as-constructed certification" (EPW 2020); monitoring to 2023 stable (Prenzler et al. 2022). Searched for top-ups, repairs, extension, damage or removal and for the effect of cyclone Alfred (March 2025): none found; the dark mound is present on the Esri image of 2025-12-01. The viewer shows the as-built state, with the caption "no later change found (searched 2026-10-05)".

2.2 How each source was used (added by the 2026-10-10 source audit)

Role: PLAN, CREST, SEABED, TIDES, VOLUME feed the model; CHECK = validation only; CONTEXT = background only; REJECTED = not used. Registry ids (palm-beach-gold-coast-img-NN) are in SOURCES_3D.md.

3. Methods

3.1 Coordinate frame, handedness and datum

The model frame is the canonical frame of shape.json: metres, origin at the foot of the perpendicular from the reef centroid to the waterline, x alongshore toward bearing beta_x = 334.3 deg true (NNW), y offshore toward beta_y = 64.3 deg true (ENE), z up with z = 0 at mean sea level (MSL). Because beta_y = beta_x + 90 deg (clockwise on a north-up map) the triple (x, y, z up) is left-handed: drawing x to the right and y up the screen mirrors the reef. The viewer therefore converts to east-north-up, which is right-handed:

E = x sin(beta_x) + y sin(beta_y)        N = x cos(beta_x) + y cos(beta_y)        U = z          (E1)
x = ( E cos(beta_y) - N sin(beta_y) ) / sin(beta_y - beta_x)     (inverse; beta_y - beta_x = 90 deg)

and draws it with three.js axes (X = E, Y = U, Z = -N), so north is up on screen in the plan preset and offshore points to the right. Check (build_3d.py, frame_check): canonical vertex 0 = (-27.98, 373.92) m is converted with (E1) and an azimuthal-equidistant projection centred on the canonical origin (-28.108526, 153.468119) (Snyder 1987) to (-28.1072903, 153.4716713); shape.json geo.polygons_latlon[0] is (-28.1072904, 153.4716713). All 47 vertices agree to 0.024 m (mean 0.016 m); with x mirrored the mean error is 82.4 m. The earlier geom.py make-canonical rotation bug (fixed 2026-10-05) is not involved: the canonical block was built by an explicit rotation and re-verified in VERIFY.md.

Pixel to canonical metres (aerial s7): a least-squares similarity transform of the 47 traced outline vertices to canonical.polygons_m

c = s R (p - p_mean) + c_mean       s = 0.117647 m/px (= 1/8.50),  R = rotation by 115.70 deg (no reflection; image y points down),  max residual 0.007 m   (E2)

Navionics screenshots (Web-Mercator, 256 px tiles, 982 x 655 px map window centred on the reef centroid 28.107334 S, 153.470913 E): X = 256 2^z (lon + 180)/360, Y = 256 2^z (0.5 - ln tan(pi/4 + lat/2)/(2 pi)) (E3); metres per pixel 2 pi R cos(lat) / (256 2^z) = 0.527 m at z = 18, 1.054 m at z = 17. Pixel to lon/lat by the inverse of (E3), then lon/lat to canonical by the inverse of (E1) (navionics_isolines.py).

Vertical datums. Tide planes are heights above Queensland Port Datum (LAT 1992) at the Gold Coast Seaway; with MSL = 0.88 m above LAT:

z_MSL = z_LAT - 0.88            z_LAT = z_MSL + 0.88            depth below LAT d = -z_LAT = -(z_MSL + 0.88)           (E4)
LAT -0.88, MLWS -0.66, MLWN -0.37, MHWN +0.36, MHWS +0.65, HAT +1.15 m  (heights vs MSL)
z_MSL = z_AHD - (MSL - AHD)     with MSL - AHD = 0.88 - 0.76 = 0.12 m (AHD = LAT + 0.760 m at the Seaway standard-port benchmark, MSQ 2014 "Standard port datum levels", read at the source in `07_scale/bathymetry/gold_coast/REPORT.md` section 3 and confirmed 2026-10-10; it applies at the benchmark only, so +-0.1 m at Palm Beach)

The Navionics app states no datum; the chart depth d_chart is converted by z_MSL = -d_chart - (MSL - CD) where CD is the chart datum above LAT (CD = 0 for LAT; assumption A5, tested in 4.3).

3.2 Plan shape

Toe outline: the 47-vertex polygon of shape.json (traced from the aerial s7, IoU 0.995 with the City of Gold Coast polygon, area 11,972 m2; 11,989 m2 on the 1 m model grid). Crest outline: the 8-vertex innermost contour (59.2 x 5.9 m, axis 104.8 deg true, hand-read on 3x zoom grids; the concept design gives 60 m at 105 deg).

3.3 Contour lines of the aerial (reef surface input)

The aerial carries 10 thin grey lines inside the toe outline (annotated/s7_contours_ranked_elevations.png). They are not labelled. contours_s7.py traces them in two parts, both deterministic:

  1. Line filter. Red channel, mean along a 31 px segment minus the mean of two parallel flanks at +-4.5 px, maximum over 30 orientations; lines respond 30-200, rock and foam texture < 25.
  2. Flank part (A). Along the crest outline (smoothed 12 px, arc step 0.5 px) with outward normal n(s), the response is resampled on p(s, d) = B(s) + d n(s). Line k is the ridge d_k(s) that maximises (dynamic programming, periodic in s) sum_s [ min(R, 60) - 30 - 15 (d_k - d_{k-1}) / l_loc ] - 1.0 sum_s |change of spacing between neighbouring rays| (change limited to 3 px per 0.5 px of arc), where l_loc is the local spacing of the two previous lines; the nearest-ridge prior makes a skipped line impossible, the smoothness term keeps the line smooth; fragments shorter than 16 m or with mean response < 30 are dropped; where the room left to the outline is < 1.4 x the local spacing the line has merged with the outline. Pieces whose slope exceeds 0.45 px/px (corner chamfers, foam streaks) and the 60 px nearest each end of the crest are dropped.
  3. End fans (B). From the centre of each end of the crest outline, rays 0.25 deg apart over +-80 deg about the crest axis; on the axis ray the response peaks counted outward are lines 0, 1, 2, ... and the outermost peak is the toe outline itself (E end: 12 peaks = lines 0-10 plus the outline, 12.3 m between lines 0-3 and 6.0 m thereafter; W end: lines 1-5 plus the outline, 1.9-2.5 m); each line is followed ray by ray (nearest peak within 7 px of the prediction, up to 10 missed rays) so that it keeps its number. A and B parts of one line are separated by 7-15 m (splice_check); the model interpolates across the gap.
  4. Result. 29 polylines (annotated/s7_contours_ranked_elevations.png): lines 1-5 close all round the crest, lines 6-10 peel off the outline toward the seaward end; the outline is line K + f with K = 4 ... 10.

3.4 Contour elevations and the reef surface

Assumption A3: the lines are at constant vertical interval Delta = 0.5 m and the crest outline is the crest (z_c = -1.5 m MSL):

z_k = z_c - Delta k                                                                                    (E5a)
z_toe = z_c - Delta (K + f),     f = min(1, d_K / l_K)                                                 (E5b)

where K is the number of traced lines inside the outline at that point, d_K the distance from the outline to the nearest line K and l_K the local spacing between lines K-1 and K (A4: the outline lies at most one interval below line K). Side slopes follow from the line spacing, tan(beta) = Delta / l: 6.00 m per line = 1:12 (north flank, outer east end), 2.47 m = 1:4.9 (south flank), 12.3 m = 1:25 (three lines near the crest at the east end), the concept figure's 1/12 and 1/5 (annotated/s7_side_slopes_from_line_spacing.png).

Reef surface: all line vertices (thinned to 1 m), the 427 toe-outline points (1 m apart) with their z from (E5b), and a 1 m fill of the crest slot at z_c form a point set; z_s(x, y) is the linear Delaunay interpolation of this set (Delaunay TIN, scipy.interpolate.LinearNDInterpolator; nearest-neighbour outside the convex hull). The surface is evaluated on a 1 m grid inside the toe outline.

3.5 Seabed from the Navionics chart (primary) and the toe elevations

Access. The Navionics ChartViewer (webapp.navionics.com) was decommissioned by Garmin in July 2024 and redirects to Garmin's Marine Maps viewer. In the author's own headless Chrome (OS-assigned random DevTools port, fresh profile in %TEMP%, process terminated by PID; never a shared browser) the page https://maps.garmin.com/en-US/marine opened without login, CAPTCHA or consent dialog; nothing was accepted or bypassed. The map was centred with the page's geohash key (r7j0h74ngmnv) and Leaflet setView; options: View = Map, Depth units = Meters, Chart type = SonarChart Maps or Nautical Charts, Seabed areas = Hide, Shallow shading = 0 to 10 m (navionics_capture.py; screenshots in ../src/navionics/, 44 of the 80 captured; "Garmin Navionics, not for navigation", private research copy, reuse rights unchecked).

Iso-depth lines. With "shallow shading = v" the chart paints water shallower than v blue, so the edge of the blue area is the v-metre contour. Check: the printed contour labels 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 m lie 0.5-1.2 m from the extracted lines of the same value; the SonarChart prints a label every 0.5 m (contour interval 0.5 m; the app states no interval). The 1-10 m lines (zoom 17, 1 m steps) are extracted as the boundary of the blue mask (navionics_isolines.py, blue-minus-red > 9, closing 5 px) and converted to canonical metres with (E3).

Seabed surface. Points on the iso-lines more than 25 m outside the toe outline (A6; 1,041 points, every second boundary pixel), 25 waterline anchors (y = 0, z = 0 per A7) and, in the model's "hybrid" seabed, 107 toe-outline points (every 4th, z from E5b, smoothing 0.2) are interpolated with a thin-plate spline (Duchon 1977; scipy.interpolate.RBFInterpolator, kernel r^2 ln r, smoothing 1.0)

z_b(x, y) = -d_nav(x, y) - 0.88 ,      d_nav(x_i, y_i) = v_i + CD  (v_i = iso-line value, CD = 0 for LAT) ,   rms of the fit to the lines 0.08 m   (E6)

on a 4 m grid, x -300..300, y -40..620 m (model.js, seabed.z_cm). Seaward of the 10 m line (y about 503 m) the surface is an extrapolation. Landward of the waterline a visual beach face rises at 1:15 (not surveyed). Because the reef itself bends the 4-6 m contours seaward by 47-81 m (section 4.5), the chart seabed under and within 25 m of the reef is a smooth interpolation, not a measurement.

3.6 Reef thickness, volume and the rendered surface

h = max(0, z_s - z_b);      V = sum h dA over the toe outline (1 m cells);      zr = z_b + w h,  w = smoothstep(dist_to_outline / 2.5 m)        (E7)

V is the rock envelope (voids included), 22,020 m3 (21,966 m3 with the 2.5 m edge ramp). The viewer draws zr on a 1 m grid (+0.07 m visual lift against z-fighting), colour from rock grey, lighter toward the crest, faded into the seabed colour at the edge. Rock layers (core 300-1000 kg; armour 1-8 t, crest 6-8 t; EPW 2020) are not drawn separately: no thicknesses are published.

3.7 Water, grid, camera

The water surface is a flat plane at the selected level (LAT, MLWS, MLWN, MSL, MHWN, MHWS, HAT), translucent, with the datum labels of (E4). Metre grid 10 and 50 m, 10 and 50 m scale bars, north arrow, waterline y = 0. Vertical exaggeration v (1-5x, default 1x, always displayed) multiplies z only (world.scale.y); labels are counter-scaled so text is not distorted. Photo-match mode (local image as a semi-transparent overlay; sliders for x, y, height above MSL, heading, pitch, roll, vertical FOV; the 35 mm-equivalent focal length f = 43.27 / (sqrt(1 + a^2) 2 tan(vfov/2)), a = aspect ratio, is shown) forces v = 1; the copied JSON holds the camera in the canonical frame (x, y, z above MSL) with heading as a true bearing, pitch positive up.
